docs.title: fair_shares.library.utils.calculate_relative_adjustment
docs.text:
Python
calculate_relative_adjustment(
    values: TimeseriesDataFrame | Series,
    functional_form: str = "asinh",
    exponent: float = 1.0,
    inverse: bool = True,
    normalize: bool = True,
    reference: float | Series | None = None,
    indicator: str = "indicator",
) -> TimeseriesDataFrame | Series

Calculate relative adjustment factors for allocations.

Applies a transformation to input values (e.g., GDP per capita, cumulative emissions) to produce adjustment factors. See docs/science/allocations.md for theoretical grounding.

When normalize=True (default), values are divided by a reference before transformation. The reference is the cross-country median of values unless the caller passes reference. This ensures unit invariance: multiplying all inputs by a constant (e.g., converting USD to EUR) produces identical adjustment factors, because the constant cancels in the ratio x / median(x). The asinh form needs this scale: asinh(x) is close to x below 1 and close to ln(2x) above it, so the reference sets where the curve bends. The power form is scale-free within one column: the reference multiplies every factor in that column by the same constant.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default values TimeseriesDataFrame | Series

Input values (GDP per capita, cumulative emissions, etc.)

required functional_form str

Transformation to apply. Default is "asinh" (inverse hyperbolic sine). arcsinh itself is defined on the full real line and preserves sign, but the subsequent ** (sign * exponent) step produces NaN on negative inputs and inf on zero for non-integer exponents — see the Notes section for caller responsibilities. "power" is the legacy form; values are clamped to a small epsilon for numerical safety.

'asinh' exponent float

Controls how aggressively the adjustment squashes the range. With inverse=True: exponent=1.0 gives 1/transform(x), exponent=2.0 gives 1/transform(x)², exponent=0.5 gives 1/sqrt(transform(x)). Greater exponent = more squashing.

1.0 inverse bool

If True (default), higher values -> lower relative adjustment factor. If False, higher values -> higher relative adjustment factor.

True normalize bool

If True (default), divide values by a reference before transformation to achieve unit invariance. Set to False for legacy behaviour or when inputs are already dimensionless.

True reference float | Series | None

Normalisation reference. Default None uses the cross-country median of values (per column for a DataFrame). Pass a fixed reference when values is a transformed indicator whose median moves with a parameter. The Gini income floor is the case in point: callers pass the median of the unadjusted capability indicator, so raising the floor lowers adjusted capability without moving the yardstick it is measured against.

None indicator str

Name used in the error message for missing values, such as "capability" or "responsibility".

'indicator'

Returns:

Type Description Adjustment factors with same structure as input

Raises:

Type Description AllocationError

If values contains missing values. The message names the affected countries. A missing indicator has no defensible default: filling it with zero gives asinh(0) ** -exponent, an infinite adjustment factor.

Notes

This function operationalizes both the Polluter Pays Principle (via historical responsibility adjustments over the window prior to the allocation year) and the Ability to Pay Principle (via economic capability adjustments, from the allocation year onwards).

The arcsinh function itself is defined on the full real line and preserves sign (it is odd), so negative inputs map to negative transformed values and zero maps to zero. However, the subsequent exponentiation step arcsinh(x) ** (sign * exponent) is not closed over the reals: for a non-integer real exponent (the typical case, since inverse=True is the default), numpy does not promote to complex, so negative bases yield NaN and a zero base with a negative exponent yields inf. In other words, asinh applies no clamping — callers that may pass negative values (e.g. cumulative CO2 including LULUCF sinks) or exact zeros must handle the sign upstream, either by flooring inputs at a small positive value or by using an emission basis that cannot be negative (e.g. fossil-fuel-and-industry only). The power form clamps to a small epsilon (1e-10) for numerical safety with negative exponents.

docs.title: fair_shares.library.utils.calculate_gini_adjusted_gdp
docs.text:
Python
calculate_gini_adjusted_gdp(
    total_gdps: ndarray,
    gini_coefficients: ndarray,
    income_floor: float,
    total_populations: ndarray,
    max_adjustment: float = 0.8,
) -> ndarray

Gini-adjusted GDP (capability) using the GDR development threshold.

Implements an interpretation of the Greenhouse Development Rights (GDR) framework's capability metric for entitlement allocation. Note: GDR was originally designed for burden-sharing; fair-shares adapts its capability calculation for use in an entitlement context. Only income above a development threshold counts as "ability to pay" for climate action.

For each individual, their first income_floor of annual income is exempt — it's needed for basic human development. Only the excess above the floor contributes to national capability.

Mathematical Foundation

Income is modelled as log-normal, parameterised by the Gini coefficient \(G\):

\[ \sigma = \sqrt{2} \cdot \Phi^{-1}\!\left(\frac{1 + G}{2}\right) \qquad \mu = \ln(\text{mean}) - \frac{\sigma^2}{2} \]

The proportion of the population below the floor is:

\[ p = \Phi\!\left(\frac{\ln(\text{floor}) - \mu}{\sigma}\right) \]

The income share of people below the floor (Lorenz curve) is:

\[ L(p) = \Phi\!\left(\Phi^{-1}(p) - \sigma\right) \]

National capability (aggregate above-threshold income):

\[ \text{capability} = \underbrace{\text{GDP} \times (1 - L(p))}_{\text{income of above-threshold people}} \;-\; \underbrace{\text{floor} \times (1 - p) \times N}_{\text{their exempt income (up to floor)}} \]

Where \(N\) is the total population.

Effect of Inequality

When combined with an income floor, higher Gini always increases measured capability: inequality concentrates income in the upper tail, so more national income sits above the development threshold:

Scenario (floor = $7,500/yr) Gini 0.30 Gini 0.60 Direction Rich (mean $20k) 63% of GDP 70% of GDP ↑ moderate Poor (mean $3k) 1.6% of GDP 21.5% of GDP ↑ dramatic

For poor countries, inequality is the only mechanism that creates any above-threshold income at all. At perfect equality with mean $3k, nobody exceeds $7,500 so capability is near zero.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default total_gdps ndarray

Array of total GDP values for each country.

required gini_coefficients ndarray

Array of Gini coefficients (0-1) for each country.

required income_floor float

Development threshold in currency units per capita per year. Must use the price base of total_gdps. Baer (2013) gives $7,500 on a 2005 base and $8,500 on a 2010 base.

required total_populations ndarray

Array of total population values for each country.

required max_adjustment float

Maximum reduction as a proportion of total GDP (default: 0.8). The default keeps capability at no less than 20% of GDP. The cap binds for low-income countries, where most people sit below the floor. It is a bound the inverse capability adjustment needs: the asinh factor behaves like reference / capability for small capability, so without a cap a few of the poorest countries take most of the allocation as the floor rises. Once the cap binds, the country's capability stays at (1 - max_adjustment) * GDP for every higher floor. The cap level is a values choice and decides results at high floors. Set it to 0 to switch the Gini adjustment off.

0.8

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

Array of adjusted GDP values (capability) for each country.

Python
compute_bunker_deduction(
    bunker_ts: DataFrame,
    start_year: int,
    net_zero_year: float | Sequence[float],
    historical_end_year: int | None = None,
    scenario_pathway: Series | None = None,

Compute cumulative international bunker fuel CO2 deduction.

The bunker series is observed to the last observed year and the scenario bunker pathway after it; without a pathway, later years take the last observed annual rate. The deduction is the cumulative of that series from start_year to the net-zero crossing: full years plus the fraction of the net-zero year (rcb.integrate).

docs.title: fair_shares.library.utils.data.rcb.integrate
docs.text:
Python
integrate(series: Series, start: int, end: float) -> float

Return the cumulative of a series from the start of start to end.

The series is linear between its reported years, and the value of a year is the flow over that whole year. The cumulative sums the full years from start to the year before end and adds the fraction of the year of end: the trapezoid of the line from that year to end. A net-zero crossing at end thus counts every year of the budget in full. An empty interval (end <= start) gives 0.

Raises:

Type Description DataProcessingError

If the reported years do not cover [start, end]

docs.title: fair_shares.library.utils.data.rcb.convention_gap_from_baseline
docs.text:
Python
convention_gap_from_baseline(
    nghgi_lulucf: Series,
    bm_direct: Series,
    indirect: Series,
    baseline_year: int,
    nz_year: float,
    splice_year: int,
) -> float

Return the NGHGI-minus-BM LULUCF gap of one scenario from the budget baseline.

The gap converts a budget in the bookkeeping-model (BM) convention to the national-inventory (NGHGI) convention. It covers the years that the published budget covers: the baseline year to the net-zero year of the scenario (Weber et al. 2026, Eqs. 2-3). The years before the baseline are not part of it; the rebase adds observed NGHGI LULUCF for those years.

The gap series is:

  • years up to splice_year: observed NGHGI LULUCF minus the scenario BM LULUCF (AFOLU|Direct)
  • years after splice_year: the scenario indirect flux (AFOLU|Indirect), because the direct flux cancels in the difference

and the gap is its cumulative from the baseline year to the net-zero crossing (full years plus the fraction of the net-zero year, integrate).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default nghgi_lulucf Series

Observed world NGHGI LULUCF CO2, indexed by year as a string

required bm_direct Series

AFOLU|Direct of the scenario, indexed by year as a string

required indirect Series

AFOLU|Indirect of the scenario, indexed by year as a string

required baseline_year int

First year of the published budget

required nz_year float

Net-zero crossing of the scenario (end of the gap)

required splice_year int

Last observed year of nghgi_lulucf

required

Returns:

Type Description float

The gap from baseline_year to nz_year. Zero when the net-zero crossing is at or before the baseline year.

docs.title: fair_shares.library.utils.data.rcb.calculate_budget_from_rcb
docs.text:
Python
calculate_budget_from_rcb(
    rcb_value: float,
    allocation_year: int,
    world_scenario_emissions_ts: TimeseriesDataFrame,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> float

Calculate total budget to allocate based on RCB value and allocation year.

RCB (Remaining Carbon Budget) values represent the remaining budget FROM 2020 onwards. The total budget to allocate depends on the allocation year:

  • If allocation_year < 2020: Add historical emissions (allocation_year to 2019)
  • If allocation_year == 2020: Use RCB directly
  • If allocation_year > 2020: Subtract emissions already used (2020 to allocation_year-1)

This ensures that the budget allocation is consistent regardless of which year is chosen as the allocation starting point.

All values are in Mt * CO2. RCB values are converted from Gt to Mt during preprocessing to match the units used in world_scenario_emissions_ts.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rcb_value float

Remaining Carbon Budget value in Mt CO2 (from 2020 onwards)

required allocation_year int

Year when budget allocation should start

required world_scenario_emissions_ts TimeseriesDataFrame

World scenario emissions timeseries data with year columns (in Mt CO2)

required verbose bool

Whether to print detailed calculation information (default: True)

True

Returns:

Type Description float

Total budget to allocate in Mt CO2

Raises:

Type Description DataProcessingError

If the world emissions lack any year from allocation_year to 2019 (allocation_year before 2020) or from 2020 to allocation_year - 1 (allocation_year after 2020)

docs.title: fair_shares.library.utils.data.rcb.process_rcb_to_2020_baseline
docs.text:
Python
process_rcb_to_2020_baseline(
    rcb_value: float,
    rcb_unit: str,
    rcb_baseline_year: int,
    emission_category: str,
    world_co2_ffi_emissions: DataFrame,
    world_lulucf_emissions: DataFrame | None = None,
    world_bunker_emissions: DataFrame | None = None,
    bunkers_deduction_mt: float = 0.0,
    lulucf_future_deduction_mt: float = 0.0,
    lulucf_convention_correction_mt: float = 0.0,
    target_baseline_year: int = 2020,
    source_name: str = "",
    scenario: str = "",
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, float | str | int]

Process RCB from its original baseline year to 2020 baseline with adjustments.

This function converts RCB values from any baseline year (>= 2020) to a standardized 2020 baseline. It also applies adjustments for international bunkers and LULUCF following Weber et al. (2026).

The published RCB covers total anthropogenic CO2 from its baseline year and includes international bunkers. The world CO2-FFI series excludes them, and the bunker deduction covers 2020 to net zero. The rebase therefore adds fossil emissions and bunker emissions for 2020 to (baseline_year - 1), so each bunker year from 2020 is deducted exactly once.

The rebase always uses actual observational data (e.g. PRIMAP), never scenario projections. What enters the rebase depends on the emission category:

  • co2-ffi: Rebase uses fossil CO2 only. LULUCF is omitted because it cancels algebraically with the LULUCF decomposition term. lulucf_future_deduction_mt subtracts expected future (base→NZ) BM LULUCF, converting the published total-CO2 RCB to an FFI-only RCB. lulucf_convention_correction_mt is not used for this category.
  • co2: Rebase uses fossil CO2 + observed LULUCF in the national- inventory (NGHGI) convention. lulucf_convention_correction_mt applies the NGHGI-vs-BM convention gap from the baseline year to net zero (Weber et al. 2026), which re-expresses the published budget against national-inventory accounting. lulucf_future_deduction_mt is not used for this category; the budget retains both FFI and LULUCF.

The calculation follows these steps: 1. Convert RCB from source unit to Mt * CO2e 2. If baseline_year > 2020: Add actual emissions from 2020 to (baseline_year - 1) — fossil + bunkers for co2-ffi, fossil + bunkers + NGHGI LULUCF for co2 3. Subtract bunkers deduction from 2020 to net zero (always reduces budget) 4. Apply LULUCF deduction (sign-ready from caller)

Sign convention for deduction parameters: - bunkers_deduction_mt: always positive (cumulative emissions), subtracted - lulucf_future_deduction_mt: sign-ready from caller (added directly). For co2-ffi: negated BM LULUCF → positive if LULUCF is a net source (increases fossil budget), capped at 0 if caller applies a precautionary rule. Zero for co2. - lulucf_convention_correction_mt: sign-ready from caller (added directly). For co2: the NGHGI-vs-BM convention gap from the baseline year to net zero (Weber et al. 2026), typically negative. Zero for co2-ffi.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rcb_value float

Original RCB value from the source

required rcb_unit str

Unit of the RCB value (e.g., "Gt * CO2", "Mt * CO2")

required rcb_baseline_year int

The year from which the RCB is calculated (must be >= 2020)

required emission_category str

Emission category: "co2-ffi" or "co2". Controls whether NGHGI LULUCF is included in the rebase.

required world_co2_ffi_emissions DataFrame

World-level CO2-FFI emissions timeseries with year columns (in Mt * CO2e). Excludes international bunkers.

required world_lulucf_emissions DataFrame or None

Observed world LULUCF CO2 emissions in the national-inventory (NGHGI) convention (e.g. the Melo et al. world row), with year columns (in Mt * CO2e). Used ONLY for the co2 rebase (default: None).

None world_bunker_emissions DataFrame or None

International bunker CO2 emissions timeseries with year columns (in Mt * CO2e). Required when baseline_year > 2020 and bunkers_deduction_mt is non-zero (default: None).

None bunkers_deduction_mt float

Total bunker CO2 emissions from 2020 to net zero in Mt * CO2e (default: 0.0). Always positive; subtracted from budget.

0.0 lulucf_future_deduction_mt float

Projected future (2020/base → NZ) BM LULUCF adjustment in Mt * CO2e, sign-ready (default: 0.0). Non-zero for co2-ffi only, where it subtracts LULUCF to convert a total-CO2 RCB to FFI-only.

0.0 lulucf_convention_correction_mt float

NGHGI-vs-BM convention gap from the baseline year to net zero in Mt * CO2e, sign-ready (default: 0.0). Non-zero for co2 only, where it re-expresses the budget from bookkeeping-model to NGHGI accounting.

0.0 target_baseline_year int

Target baseline year for standardization (default: 2020)

2020 source_name str

Name of the RCB source for logging (default: "")

'' scenario str

Scenario name for logging (default: "")

'' verbose bool

Whether to print detailed calculation information (default: True)

True

Returns:

Type Description dict

Dictionary containing: - 'rcb_2020_mt': RCB adjusted to 2020 baseline in Mt * CO2e - 'rcb_original_value': Original RCB value (in source units) - 'rcb_original_unit': Original RCB unit - 'baseline_year': Original baseline year - 'rebase_total_mt': Emissions added to rebase from source year to 2020 (positive, Mt * CO2e); fossil + bunkers for co2-ffi, fossil + bunkers + observed NGHGI LULUCF for co2 - 'rebase_fossil_mt': Fossil-only component of rebase (Mt * CO2e) - 'rebase_bunkers_mt': International bunker component of rebase (Mt * CO2e) - 'rebase_lulucf_mt': Observed NGHGI LULUCF component of rebase (Mt * CO2e); only non-zero for co2 - 'deduction_bunkers_mt': Bunker fuel deduction (negative, Mt * CO2e) - 'deduction_lulucf_future_mt': projected-LULUCF deduction applied to convert total-CO2 → FFI-only. Non-zero for co2-ffi, zero for co2. - 'correction_lulucf_convention_mt': NGHGI-vs-BM convention correction. Non-zero for co2, zero for co2-ffi. - 'net_adjustment_mt': Total change from original to 2020 baseline (rebase + deductions + correction, Mt * CO2e)

Raises:

Type Description DataProcessingError

If a timeseries lacks a year of the rebase, or if baseline_year > 2020 and bunkers are deducted without world_bunker_emissions

docs.title: fair_shares.library.utils.math.convergence.validate_convergence_speed
docs.text:
Python
validate_convergence_speed(
    convergence_speed: float,
    sorted_columns: list,
    start_column: str | int | float,
    year_fraction_of_cumulative_emissions: Series,
    initial_shares: Series,
    target_cumulative_shares: Series,
) -> tuple[bool, Series | None]

Validate that a convergence_speed produces valid shares hitting cumulative targets.

We need yearly shares to transition from initial_shares (yearly share for starting year) to eventually satisfy target_cumulative_shares (cumulative sum of yearly shares of emissions over all years for each country).

So the constraint is that the cumulative sum of yearly shares of emissions over all years must equal the cumulative target shares for each country:

Text Only
sum_t [year_fraction_of_cumulative_emissions(t) * yearly_share(t)]
    = target_cumulative_shares

where: - year_fraction_of_cumulative_emissions(t): fraction of total cumulative world emissions that occur in year t for each country (sums to 1) - yearly_share(t): each country's yearly allocation share in year t (sums to 1) - target_cumulative_shares: cumulative target (sum of yearly shares of emissions over all years for each country, sums to 1)

Since we want to converge, rather than jump instantly, we model this using an exponential decay where each year's share moves toward a long_run_shares value:

Text Only
yearly_share(t+1) = yearly_share(t) + speed * (long_run_shares
    - yearly_share(t))

where: - speed: convergence rate (0 = no change, 1 = instant jump) - long_run_shares: asymptotic year share that each year converges toward (not cumulative - this is a single asymptotic year value) - initial_shares: yearly share for the starting year (year 0)

By using the exponential decay convergence function we reduce the problem from N unknowns to 1 unknown (long_run_shares). We know initial_shares, convergence_speed (which determines how fast initial_shares decay as (1-speed)^t), and target_cumulative_shares. So, we can calculate how much of the cumulative target shares comes from initial_shares (w = total_initial_contribution, accounting for their decaying contribution to cumulative target shares over time). The rest (1-w) must come from long_run_shares, so we solve: long_run_shares = (target_cumulative_shares - initial_shares*w) / (1-w).

The convergence speed is valid only if long_run_shares are all in [0, 1] (each country's share is valid). Note: if initial_shares and target_cumulative_shares both sum to 1, then long_run_shares automatically sums to 1 (mathematically guaranteed), so we only need to check individual bounds. The intuition for the [0, 1] bound is that if long_run_shares are not in [0, 1], then the speed is invalid because it would require impossible destinations (negative or >100%) to compensate, which would occur over the finite time horizon we care about.

The caller uses this function to find the minimum valid speed: the smoothest transition that still achieves cumulative targets.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default convergence_speed float

The convergence speed to validate (0 to 1).

required sorted_columns list

Year columns in sorted order.

required start_column str | int | float

Column label for first allocation year.

required year_fraction_of_cumulative_emissions Series

Fraction of cumulative emissions in each year (sums to 1).

required initial_shares Series

Initial emission shares at start year.

required target_cumulative_shares Series

Target cumulative shares to achieve.

required

Returns:

Type Description tuple[bool, Series | None]

(is_valid, long_run_shares) where: - is_valid: boolean indicating whether the speed is valid - long_run_shares: yearly share value that satisfies the cumulative constraint where long_run_shares is not used anywhere but just reported.

docs.title: fair_shares.library.utils.calculate_exponential_decay_pathway
docs.text:
Python
calculate_exponential_decay_pathway(
    total_budget: float,
    start_value: float,
    start_year: int,
    end_year: int,
    tolerance: float = 1e-06,
) -> Series

Generate an exponential decay emission pathway that sums to a total budget.

Creates a pathway following normalized shifted exponential decay that reaches exactly zero at the end year:

Text Only
E(t) = start_value * (e^(-k*t) - e^(-k*T)) / (1 - e^(-k*T))

where k is solved such that the discrete sum of annual emissions equals the total budget. The normalization factor (1 - e^(-k*T)) ensures:

  • E(0) = start_value (preserves initial year emissions)
  • E(T) = 0 (reaches exactly zero at end year)
  • Sum over all years equals total_budget

This is more appropriate for RCB-derived pathways than standard exponential decay which asymptotically approaches (but never reaches) zero, ensuring the budget is fully consumed by the end year.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default total_budget float

Total cumulative emissions budget to distribute over the pathway. Must be positive.

required start_value float

Initial emission rate at start_year (E(t_0)). Must be positive.

required start_year int

First year of the pathway (t_0).

required end_year int

Last year of the pathway (T), inclusive.

required tolerance float

Relative tolerance for budget conservation verification. Default is 1e-6.

1e-06

Returns:

Type Description Series

Annual emissions pathway indexed by year (as strings). Values represent emissions for each year.

Raises:

Type Description AllocationError

If inputs are invalid, no solution exists, or budget constraint cannot be satisfied.

Examples:

Python Console Session
>>> pathway = calculate_exponential_decay_pathway(
...     total_budget=1000.0, start_value=50.0, start_year=2020, end_year=2050
... )
>>> abs(pathway.sum() - 1000.0) < 0.01
True

Bases: BaseModel

Validates allocation output data after allocation runs.

This model ensures allocation outputs are mathematically valid and complete:

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Bug reports, allocation approaches, data sources, documentation fixes and reproductions of published studies are all welcome.

docs.title: Reporting issues
docs.text: Open an issue at github.com/setupelz/fair-shares/issues. Say what you ran (notebook, API call or snakemake invocation, with its sources and target), what you expected, what happened (the full traceback), and your Python version and install method. For numbers that look wrong, name the approach, the emission category and the affected countries and years.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Bash
git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fair-shares.git
cd fair-shares
uv sync --extra dev
uv run pre-commit install

Notebooks are jupytext .py files. Edit the .py, never the .ipynb, and regenerate with make sync-ipynb.

docs.title: Making a change
docs.text:
1. Fork, and branch from main (for example fix/lulucf-year-bounds).
  2. Change code and tests together. Allocation logic needs a test that pins the expected numbers.
  3. Run make test and make lint (make lint-fix fixes what it can). Pre-commit runs ruff and checks 80% docstring coverage.
  4. For docs changes, run uv run mkdocs build --strict (Docs conventions).
  5. Open a pull request that says what changed and why. If allocation results change, name the approaches and categories.

Docstrings follow the numpy convention and are the authoritative description of behaviour, because the API pages are generated from them. A behaviour change changes the docstring in the same commit.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Year columns are strings: df["2020"], never df[2020]. Call ensure_string_year_columns(df) after loading data.
  • Kebab-case for configuration, snake_case for Python: equal-per-capita-budget names the approach, equal_per_capita_budget the function.
  • Index levels: emissions use iso3c, unit, emission-category. GDP, population and Gini use iso3c, unit.

docs.title: Where the code lives
docs.text:
Module Location Responsibility Allocations src/fair_shares/library/allocations/ Core allocation functions Utilities src/fair_shares/library/utils/ Data manipulation, adjustments Config src/fair_shares/library/config/ Pydantic models Preprocessing src/fair_shares/library/preprocessing/ Reusable logic for the 100-series preprocessing notebooks Pipeline src/fair_shares/library/pipeline/ Composite, RCB, pathway and non-CO2 preprocessing runners IAMC history src/fair_shares/library/iamc_historical/ Back-fills IAM scenarios with IAMC-consistent historical emissions Python API src/fair_shares/library/python_api.py Computes allocation timeseries in memory, without notebooks Presets src/fair_shares/library/presets/ Parameter grids of published studies (ESABCC 2023 / PRR2023) Data fetch src/fair_shares/library/data_fetch.py Downloads registry files and checks their checksums Citations src/fair_shares/library/citations.py Derives and formats the citations a run needs Data registry src/fair_shares/library/data_registry.py Reads and checks conf/data_registry.yaml (source, licence, citation) Notebooks notebooks/1xx_*.py Data pipeline notebooks

Architecture follows one budget run and one pathway run through this code.

docs.title: New approaches and data sources
docs.text:
Every allocation approach expresses a set of equity principles. Before you add one, read From principle to code and work through the five entry points of Pelz 2025b.

Three points from the literature apply to every new approach:

  • No approach is value-neutral. Every allocation choice embeds normative judgements Dooley 2021; Kartha 2018.
  • Grandfathering has no philosophical support and conflicts with the purpose of equity analysis Dooley 2021; Kartha 2018.
  • Contradictory principles do not combine into a coherent result Dooley 2021.

Then follow Adding approaches or Adding data sources. A new data source needs a registry entry, a verified DOI record and a CITATION.md (Registering the source).

docs.title: Adding Allocation Approaches
docs.text: This guide explains how to add new allocation approaches to fair-shares.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Allocation approaches live in two directories:

Type Location Output Budget allocations/budgets/ Single cumulative allocation Pathway allocations/pathways/ Time-varying annual allocations

Each approach is registered in get_allocation_functions() in allocations/manager.py.

docs.title: Before You Begin
docs.text:
Every allocation approach operationalizes specific equity principles. Before writing code, you should be able to explain:

  1. What equity principle(s) it implements
  2. What value judgments are embedded
  3. How it relates to existing approaches

If unclear, read Principle-to-Code first.

Value neutrality

Do not present the approach as value-neutral: all allocation choices embed normative judgments Dooley 2021; Kartha 2018.

Use the Entry Points Framework to structure your normative documentation: (1) foundational principles, (2) allocation quantity, (3) allocation approach, (4) indicators, (5) implications for all others Pelz 2025b. See From Principle to Code.

Grandfathering

Grandfathering assigns shares in proportion to current emissions. It has no support in the equity literature and conflicts with the normative basis of this library Dooley 2021; Kartha 2018. Contraction-and-convergence approaches that start from current national emissions embed grandfathering during the convergence period, so the same applies to them Kartha 2018. Ground a new approach in the equity principles documented in From Principle to Code.

docs.title: Contribution Workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Identify Principles] --> B[Implement Function]
    B --> C[Export]
    C --> D[Register]
    D --> E[Add Tests]
    E --> F[Update Docs if Needed]

Key principles:

  1. Know your principles first - You should be able to explain what equity principle the approach implements before writing code
  2. Docstrings include math - Document the mathematical foundation in the docstring (see existing approaches for examples)
  3. Tests validate behavior - Tests should verify both correctness and that parameters have expected effects
  4. Registration makes it discoverable - Until registered, the approach cannot be used via the high-level API

docs.title: Function Signature
docs.text:
All allocation functions follow a consistent pattern:

Python
def my_new_budget(
    # Required data
    population_ts: TimeseriesDataFrame,
    allocation_year: int,
    emission_category: str,
    # Optional data (for adjustments)
    country_actual_emissions_ts: TimeseriesDataFrame | None = None,
    gdp_ts: TimeseriesDataFrame | None = None,
    # Parameters specific to this approach
    my_parameter: float = 0.5,
    # Common parameters
    group_level: str = "iso3c",
    unit_level: str = "unit",
) -> BudgetAllocationResult:
    """Docstring with academic context."""
    ...

docs.title: Required Return Type
docs.text:
• Budget approaches: BudgetAllocationResult
  • Pathway approaches: PathwayAllocationResult

Both are dataclasses in allocations/results/.

docs.title: Budget Example
docs.text:
Create a new file or add to existing module in allocations/budgets/:

Python
"""My new allocation approach."""

from fair_shares.library.allocations.results import BudgetAllocationResult
from fair_shares.library.validation.models import AllocationInputs, AllocationOutputs


def my_new_budget(
    population_ts,
    allocation_year: int,
    emission_category: str,
    my_parameter: float = 0.5,
    group_level: str = "iso3c",
    unit_level: str = "unit",
) -> BudgetAllocationResult:
    """
    Allocate budget using my new approach.

    This approach does X based on principle Y from Author (Year).

    Parameters
    ----------
    population_ts : TimeseriesDataFrame
        Population data with MultiIndex (iso3c, unit)
    allocation_year : int
        Year when allocation begins
    emission_category : str
        Emission category being allocated
    my_parameter : float, default 0.5
        Controls strength of adjustment

    Returns
    -------
    BudgetAllocationResult
        Contains relative_shares_cumulative_emission

    See Also
    --------
    docs/science/allocations.md : Theoretical grounding
    """
    # Validate inputs
    AllocationInputs(
        population_ts=population_ts,
        first_allocation_year=allocation_year,
        last_allocation_year=allocation_year,
        group_level=group_level,
        unit_level=unit_level,
    )

    # Calculate shares (must sum to 1)
    # ... your implementation ...

    relative_shares = calculate_shares(population_ts, allocation_year, my_parameter)

    # Validate outputs
    AllocationOutputs(
        shares=relative_shares,
        dataset_name="my-new-budget allocation",
    )

    # Return result
    return BudgetAllocationResult(
        approach="my-new-budget",
        relative_shares_cumulative_emission=relative_shares,
        parameters={
            "allocation_year": allocation_year,
            "my_parameter": my_parameter,
        },
    )

docs.title: Key Implementation Details
docs.text:
1. Validate inputs using AllocationInputs Pydantic model. Pass the function's group_level and unit_level, and set country_emissions_read_at_first_year=True when the approach reads country emissions at the first allocation year
  2. Shares must sum to 1 for each group (e.g., climate-assessment, quantile)
  3. Validate outputs using AllocationOutputs model
  4. Document thoroughly with academic citations (see Docs conventions for required structure)

docs.title: Step 3: Export the Function
docs.text:
Add to the module's __init__.py:

Python
# allocations/budgets/__init__.py
from fair_shares.library.allocations.budgets.my_module import my_new_budget

__all__ = [
    "equal_per_capita_budget",
    "per_capita_adjusted_budget",
    "per_capita_adjusted_gini_budget",
    "my_new_budget",  # Add here
]

docs.title: Step 4: Register the Approach
docs.text:
Add the approach to get_allocation_functions() in allocations/manager.py:

Python
from fair_shares.library.allocations.budgets import (
    # ... existing imports ...
    my_new_budget,
)

def get_allocation_functions() -> dict[str, Callable[..., Any]]:
    return {
        # ... existing approaches ...
        "my-new-budget": my_new_budget,
    }

docs.title: Step 5: Add Tests
docs.text:
Create tests in tests/unit/allocations/:

Python
from fair_shares.library.utils import create_example_data


def test_my_new_budget_basic():
    """Test basic functionality."""
    data = create_example_data()
    result = my_new_budget(
        population_ts=data["population"],
        allocation_year=2020,
        emission_category="co2-ffi",
    )

    # Shares sum to 1
    shares = result.relative_shares_cumulative_emission["2020"]
    assert abs(shares.sum() - 1.0) < 1e-10

    # Result type
    assert result.approach == "my-new-budget"


def test_my_new_budget_parameter_effect():
    """Test that parameter has expected effect."""
    data = create_example_data()
    result_low = my_new_budget(
        population_ts=data["population"],
        allocation_year=2020,
        emission_category="co2-ffi",
        my_parameter=0.0,
    )
    result_high = my_new_budget(
        population_ts=data["population"],
        allocation_year=2020,
        emission_category="co2-ffi",
        my_parameter=1.0,
    )

    # Verify parameter affects results as expected
    assert result_low.approach == "my-new-budget"
    assert result_high.approach == "my-new-budget"

Key test assertions:

  • Shares sum to 1.0: abs(shares.sum() - 1.0) < 1e-10
  • Approach name matches registry key
  • Parameters stored in result object

  2. Science docs - Add to docs/science/allocations.md if introducing new principle
  3. API docs - Auto-generated from docstrings

Please consider the following:

  • Explicit statement or link to documentation regarding normative foundations
  • Indicator choices and justifications

docs.title: Adding data sources
docs.text:
A data source is an entry in src/fair_shares/conf/data_sources/data_sources_unified.yaml, a registry entry, and a preprocessing notebook in the notebooks/1xx_*.py series. A new release of a source the library already uses is simpler: see Updating data each year.

Type Purpose Current sources emissions Historical emissions without land use PRIMAP-hist v2.8 primap-202609 (default), v2.6.1 primap-202503, Global Carbon Budget 2025 gcb-2025 gdp Capability World Bank WDI population Per capita calculations UN/OWID gini Inequality within countries World Bank WDI (default), UNU-WIDER WIID lulucf National-inventory land-use CO₂ Melo et al. (2026): melo-2026-v4 (default), melo-2026 targets Global limits AR6 scenarios, remaining carbon budgets scenario sources Scenario-derived budget terms ar6, sci in src/fair_shares/conf/scenario_sources.yaml

docs.title: 1. Place the raw data
docs.text: Put the files in data/<type>/<source>-<year>/, for example data/emissions/my-source-2026/. The {source}-{year} name versions the source.

docs.title: 2. Configure the source
docs.text:
Add an entry to src/fair_shares/conf/data_sources/data_sources_unified.yaml:

YAML
# Example: Adding a new emissions source
emissions:
  primap-202609:
    # ... existing source ...

  my-source-2026: # New source
    path: "data/emissions/my-source-2026/emissions_data.csv"
    data_parameters:
      available_categories:
        - co2-ffi
        - all-ghg
      world_key: "WORLD" # How the source identifies global totals
      scenario: "HISTCR" # Optional: historical scenario identifier
      bunkers_source: "gcb-2025" # Optional: registry name of the bunker data
      # Optional: coverage rule for analysis countries
      coverage: { emissions_recorded_before: 1990, population_from: 1850 }

docs.title: Common Configuration Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Purpose path Relative path to data file available_categories Which emission categories this source provides world_key String used to identify global totals in the data scenario Optional. Historical scenario, for sources that have one bunkers_source Optional. Bunker data paired with an emissions source (default gcb-2025) coverage Optional. Coverage rule for analysis countries (default: none)

The pipeline asks an emissions source only for the categories in available_categories. A source that declares co2-ffi alone, such as gcb-2025, runs one pass of its notebook 101 and supports co2-ffi runs.

By default, an analysis country has complete emissions, GDP and population from 1990 through the last year of each dataset. A coverage block adds two tests, and a country that fails either one joins rest-of-world. emissions_recorded_before requires a value in the raw emissions file in a year before the threshold. population_from requires population for every year from the threshold. A source that zero-fills blank years needs the first test, because a blank and a reported zero look the same after the fill. Its notebook 101 writes emiss_<category>_first_recorded_year.csv (columns iso3c, first_recorded_year) for each category it provides. The rule is coverage_exclusions in src/fair_shares/library/preprocessing/coverage.py. country_data_coverage_summary.csv names the failed test for each country in the column coverage_rule_failed. A source without the block keeps the default check alone, and its coverage summary has no such column. gcb-2025 sets both tests.

docs.title: Registering the source
docs.text:
Every new source needs three things:

  1. Registry entry. Add it to src/fair_shares/conf/data_registry.yaml with its URL, checksum, licence, citation and tier. default sources download with a plain fetch-data, optional ones with --all, and manual ones print instructions for a file the user places. State in a comment what the licence means for outputs, as the primap-202609 entry does. tests/unit/test_data_registry.py fails if a source lacks a licence or citation, or if a data/ path in the config has no registry entry. A registered source downloads on first use.
  2. Verified DOI. Look up each DOI the entry claims at DataCite, Crossref or doi.org. Record it in tests/fixtures/verified_dois.yaml with the evidence and the date. test_data_registry.py and test_citations.py fail on any DOI missing from that file. uv run pytest -m network re-resolves the recorded DOIs (test_dois_resolve.py).
  3. CITATION.md. Place one in the source's data folder with the full citation, DOI and licence, as the existing sources do.

Assert only a DOI or licence you have verified upstream. A source with no DOI gets name-only credit.

docs.title: 3. Write the preprocessing notebook
docs.text:
The Snakefile builds the notebook name from the source key: 101_data_preprocess_emiss_{source}.py for emissions and 108_data_preprocess_bunkers_{bunkers_source}.py for bunkers. An emissions entry with a notebook key names the notebook instead. Both PRIMAP-hist entries set notebook: "101_data_preprocess_emiss_primap", so a new PRIMAP release needs a config entry and a registry entry and no new notebook.

The notebook reads the path in the config and writes to the run's intermediate directory, which the Snakefile sets through source_id:

Python
import pandas as pd
from pyprojroot import here
from fair_shares.library.utils import ensure_string_year_columns

df = pd.read_csv(here() / "data/emissions/my-source-2026/emissions_data.csv")
df["iso3c"] = convert_to_iso3c(df["country_column"])          # your country-code mapping
df = df.set_index(["iso3c", "unit", "emission-category"])
df = ensure_string_year_columns(df)

if "World" not in df.index.get_level_values("iso3c"):        # add a World row if missing
    world = df.groupby(["unit", "emission-category"]).sum()
    world["iso3c"] = "World"
    df = pd.concat([df, world.set_index("iso3c", append=True)])

out = here() / f"output/{source_id}/intermediate/emissions/emiss_co2-ffi_timeseries.csv"
out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
df.to_csv(out)

Every output follows one index structure, with year columns as strings ("1990"):

Data Index levels Columns Emissions iso3c, unit, emission-category Years GDP, population iso3c, unit Years Gini iso3c, unit gini (one value, not time-varying)

A new source should cover at least the major emitters, include a World total, use standard units (Mt CO₂e for emissions, million for population) and document its gaps.

docs.title: 4. Test
docs.text:
Run the preprocessing notebook, then an allocation that names the new source in active_sources of notebook 301. Check the country coverage and year ranges in country_data_coverage_summary.csv.

These notebooks are good models:

Notebook Type Example of 101_data_preprocess_emiss_primap.py Emissions NetCDF processing, category mapping, one notebook for every release 101_data_preprocess_emiss_gcb-2025.py Emissions Long CSV, single category, logic in one library function 102_data_preprocess_gdp_wdi-2025.py GDP CSV processing, country code mapping 103_data_preprocess_population_un-owid-2025.py Population Combining historical and projected data 105_data_preprocess_gini_wdi-2025.py Gini Latest value in a window, filtering aggregates 105_data_preprocess_gini_unu-wider-2025.py Gini Quality filtering, stationary output 107_derive_lulucf_categories.py Land use National-inventory corrections, metadata, world totals

docs.title: Land-use sources
docs.text:
National-inventory land-use CO₂ replaces the bookkeeping estimates in PRIMAP. Total CO₂ (co2) and all-ghg need it (Convention gap).

Notebook 107 serves every land-use source and receives active_lulucf_source as a papermill parameter. It writes:

  • emiss_co2-lulucf_lu_timeseries.csv: country land-use CO₂ (the PRIMAP bookkeeping version from notebook 101 keeps its base filename);
  • world_co2-lulucf_timeseries.csv: the world total for the budget corrections;
  • lulucf_metadata.yaml: the year bounds and the files written.

To add a source, place it in data/lulucf/{source-name}/ and add an entry under lulucf: with data_parameters: format, iso3_column, year_column, value_column, category_filter, gas_filter and exclude_regions. The notebook reads the release label from the file name (..._v3.1.csv, ..._4.0.0.csv), so the name must end in a version number.

Allocations in co2 and all-ghg start no earlier than the first year of the land-use data. Both Melo releases start in 2000.

Category Uses land-use data Why co2-ffi No Fossil fuels only co2 Yes Country co2 = co2-ffi + national-inventory co2-lulucf on shared years. Bunkers enter only at world and budget level all-ghg Yes Splits into co2 and non-co2 all-ghg-ex-co2-lulucf No Its CO₂ part is co2-ffi co2-lulucf Indirectly It is the land-use data non-co2 No Derived by subtraction

Notebook 108 (rule preprocess_bunkers) writes bunker_timeseries.csv, the international bunker emissions.

docs.title: Scenario sources and budgets
docs.text:
Scenario pathways must already be internally consistent with the emissions convention. The pipeline corrects the budgets, not the pathways. The Gidden et al. AR6 reanalysis is consistent with PRIMAP history. A custom scenario source in another convention needs its corrections in its preprocessing notebook before the data enter the pipeline.

Every scenario source maps its categories to the normalised climate-assessment and quantile fields; AR6 maps C1 to 1.5C and 0.5. A new source must write these columns. Notebook 104 is the reference. A new scenario source is an entry in src/fair_shares/conf/scenario_sources.yaml that declares the world variables, metadata columns and bunker variables notebook 104 reads, and the budget terms it supplies.

An all-GHG budget run splits into a CO₂ budget and a non-CO₂ pathway. Notebook 104 builds the non-CO₂ pathway of each budget from its own scenario set (the temperature-matched set, or the AR6 category under scenario_selection: ar6-category), and non-CO₂ rows carry the budget's source key. A new budget label needs at least min_scenarios scenarios in each of its sets, or notebook 104 raises a ConfigurationError that names it. data/rcbs/rcbs.yaml lists the labels left out of the defaults and why (Decomposition; Architecture).

docs.title: Normative implications
docs.text:
Some data source choices carry normative weight. Contributors should document the rationale for their data source choices. For example, some decision points include:

  • GDP: PPP vs. MER measurement can significantly affect allocation results. PPP tends to raise developing-country capacity shares Pelz 2025b.
  • Emissions: Production vs. consumption accounting embeds different theories of responsibility. Production accounting (territorial) excludes embedded imports; consumption accounting includes them.
  • Population: Projection method choices (UN median, SSP scenarios) affect per capita allocations, particularly for countries with high projected growth.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This page traces one allocation from the notebook configuration cell to the parquet file on disk. Read it before changing the code. The Pipeline map lists every stage, notebook and output file, and the Science pages explain the equity principles.

docs.title: Layer map
docs.text:
A request flows down the layers, and data flows back up.

Layer Module Responsibility Entry points 0 Notebook notebooks/301_custom_fair_share_allocation.py Configuration, data pipeline trigger, plots "Configuration (edit this)" and "Execution (Run All from here)" 1 Helpers notebook_helpers.py Load data, run every allocation, print a summary load_allocation_data(), run_all_allocations(), run_and_save_category_allocations() 2 Manager allocations/manager.py Approach registry, parameter grid, single dispatch, saving, budget or pathway classification run_parameter_grid(), run_allocation(), get_function(), is_budget_approach() 3 Maths allocations/budgets/per_capita.py, allocations/pathways/*.py Population shares and the responsibility and capability adjustments _per_capita_budget_core(), equal_per_capita_budget()

The maths returns relative shares in two containers from allocations/results/__init__.py: BudgetAllocationResult (relative_shares_cumulative_emission, one year column) and PathwayAllocationResult (relative_shares_pathway_emissions, one column per year). Each column sums to 1.0. The helpers multiply shares by a global budget or pathway later. The same allocation therefore applies to any budget estimate or scenario without rerunning the maths.

The manager classifies an approach as a budget approach when its name ends in -budget. Keep that convention for new approaches.

docs.title: Example 1: a co2-ffi budget
docs.text:
Notebook 301 configured with:

Python
emission_category = "co2-ffi"
active_sources = {"target": "rcbs", ...}
allocations = {
    "equal-per-capita-budget": [{"allocation_year": [2015], "preserve_allocation_year_shares": [False]}]
}

docs.title: 1. Data pipeline
docs.text:
The notebook calls setup_data() (utils/data/setup.py). It:

  1. validates the configuration with build_data_config() (utils/data/config.py), which reads conf/data_sources/data_sources_unified.yaml and checks it with Pydantic (config/models.py);
  2. builds the paths and the Snakemake command;
  3. compares the provenance stamp output/<source_id>/.provenance_stamp.json (utils/data/provenance.py) with fresh hashes. A missing or different stamp adds --forceall and logs what changed. FAIR_SHARES_TRUST_CACHE=1 or trust_cache=True skips the check. The check needs a checkout, so an installed package reuses a prebuilt tree as it is;
  4. runs Snakemake when files are missing or the stamp differs, and writes a fresh stamp after a successful run.

The Snakefile runs the preprocessing notebooks in dependency order and ends with the master notebook, 100_data_preprocess_rcbs for budgets (MASTER_NOTEBOOKS). With active_scenario_source: ar6, notebook 104 also selects the scenario sets of every budget (utils/data/scenario_sets.py) and writes rcb_scenario_adjustments.yaml, one scenario_set_{source}_{label}.csv per budget and bunker_share_reporters.csv. The processed CSVs land in output/<source_id>/intermediate/processed/.

docs.title: 2. Load data
docs.text:
load_allocation_data() reads the processed CSVs:

  • emissions_data["co2-ffi"]: country emissions indexed by iso3c, unit, emission-category;
  • rcbs_data["co2-ffi"]: one row per budget with source, climate-assessment, quantile and rcb_2020_mt, plus each budget's deductions and the provenance of its scenario sets;
  • world_emissions_data["co2-ffi"]: world history, which converts a budget from 2020 to a budget from the allocation year;
  • GDP, population and Gini, validated.

docs.title: 3. Run allocations
docs.text:
run_all_allocations() splits the approaches into budget and pathway with is_budget_approach(), loops over final_categories (here only co2-ffi) and calls run_and_save_category_allocations().

_run_budget_allocations() calls run_parameter_grid() once per category, because shares depend only on the socioeconomic data and the parameters. Then, for each budget row, it:

  1. converts the budget from 2020 to a budget from the allocation year with calculate_budget_from_rcb();
  2. multiplies the shares by it with BudgetAllocationResult.get_absolute_budgets();
  3. saves the result with save_allocation_result().

docs.title: 4. Parameter grid and dispatch
docs.text:
run_parameter_grid() validates the target and allocation years, converts kebab-case keys to snake_case, and expands each list into combinations with _expand_parameters() (itertools.product; here one combination). run_allocation() then:

  1. looks up the function with get_function("equal-per-capita-budget");
  2. checks the user's parameters against the function signature. An unknown parameter raises AllocationError that names the approach, the rejected parameters and the accepted ones, so every configured parameter reaches the approach;
  3. passes the data frames the function accepts (validate_function_parameters(), filter_function_parameters()) and calls it.

docs.title: 5. Maths
docs.text: equal_per_capita_budget() calls _per_capita_budget_core() with both weights at 0.0. It filters population to the allocation year onwards, converts units, sums each country's population, divides by the world total, applies max_deviation_sigma if set, and returns a BudgetAllocationResult.

docs.title: 6. Saving
docs.text: save_allocation_result() (manager.py) hands over to results/serializers.py. It adds metadata columns from results/metadata.py and appends rows to allocations_relative.parquet and allocations_absolute.parquet. After the last budget row, create_param_manifest() writes param_manifest.csv, and generate_readme() the README files.

docs.title: Example 2: an all-ghg budget
docs.text:
The same configuration with emission_category = "all-ghg". A remaining carbon budget limits CO₂ only, so the run splits into a CO₂ budget and a non-CO₂ pathway. utils/data/config.py decides this: is_composite_category("all-ghg") and needs_decomposition("rcbs", "all-ghg") are True, and get_final_categories("rcbs", "all-ghg") returns ("co2", "non-co2").

Pipeline. The Snakefile preprocesses emissions for co2-ffi, co2, co2-lulucf and all-ghg-ex-co2-lulucf, and scenarios for co2-ffi and all-ghg-ex-co2-lulucf. It derives non-CO₂ by subtraction (rules derive_non_co2_emissions, derive_non_co2_scenarios): all-ghg-ex-co2-lulucf - co2-ffi. In budget mode the subtraction runs on the median pathway of each budget's non-CO₂ set, so non-CO₂ rows carry the budget's source. The master step runs twice: 100_data_preprocess_rcbs for co2 and 100_data_preprocess_pathways for non-co2.

Auto-derived pathway approaches. You define only budget approaches. run_all_allocations() derives the pathway approaches with derive_pathway_allocations() (manager.py), which maps each budget approach to its pathway form and renames or drops budget-only parameters (the mapping).

Category loop. The co2 pass follows example 1. The non-co2 pass calls _run_pathway_allocations(), which groups scenarios by climate-assessment, quantile and, for budget runs, source, takes each group's world pathway, runs the grid, and multiplies year-by-year shares by the pathway with PathwayAllocationResult.get_absolute_emissions(). The pathway maths (pathways/per_capita.py, _per_capita_core()) uses first_allocation_year and returns one column per year. With preserve_first_allocation_year_shares=False, each year's shares follow that year's population.

Scenario labels. Notebook 104 maps each scenario source's categories to normalised climate-assessment and quantile fields, and downstream code reads only these (Scenario labels).

Missing pathways. A budget label whose non-CO₂ set holds fewer than min_scenarios scenarios raises a ConfigurationError in notebook 104 that names the label. The Python API raises a ValueError when a budget row has no non-CO₂ pathway (Decomposition).

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text:
Module Location Purpose DataPreprocessor pipeline/preprocessing.py Load, validate, filter to analysis countries, add rest of world run_rcb_preprocessing() pipeline/preprocessing.py Budget corrections and processing run_pathway_preprocessing() pipeline/preprocessing.py Scenario loading and processing run_composite_preprocessing() pipeline/preprocessing.py The two passes of an all-GHG run run_non_co2_preprocessing() pipeline/preprocessing.py Non-CO₂ by subtraction, then pathway processing

DataPreprocessor keeps the countries with complete emissions, GDP and population from 1990 and adds a rest-of-world row: the world total minus those countries. Allocations therefore cover all global emissions. Gini does not decide membership. A country without a Gini value stays in and gets an imputed value under general.gini_missing_policy (default fallback-mean). An emissions source can add a coverage rule (coverage_exclusions in preprocessing/coverage.py; Analysis countries).

Text Only
output/<source_id>/
  .provenance_stamp.json        input hashes; decides reuse or rebuild
  config.yaml                   validated configuration
  notebooks/                    executed preprocessing notebooks
  intermediate/
    emissions/                  per-category CSVs, world_co2-lulucf_timeseries.csv,
                                bunker_timeseries.csv, lulucf_metadata.yaml
    gdp/  population/  gini/
    scenarios/                  scenario timeseries; budget mode adds rcb_scenario_adjustments.yaml,
                                scenario_set_*.csv, bunker_share_reporters.csv

Outputs documents the allocation files.

docs.title: Docs conventions
docs.text: Documentation must match the code. When they conflict, the code is correct and the docs are wrong.

docs.title: Where each fact lives
docs.text:
Layer Location Source of truth for Docstrings src/fair_shares/library/ What the code does: maths, parameters, return types Science docs docs/science/ Why it works this way: equity principles, citations, design rationale How-to and reference docs/user-guide/, docs/reproductions/ How to use it: workflows, examples, file and column reference API docs docs/api/ Generated from docstrings by mkdocstrings

How-to pages may simplify, but only when the simplification stays accurate. If an API page is wrong, fix the docstring. State each fact once and link to it from elsewhere.

docs.title: Writing style
docs.text:
• Short sentences, one idea each, active voice and plain words.
  • No em-dashes and no icons.
  • State what is true now. Leave revision history and provenance notes to the changelog and commits.
  • Name every source with a verified citation.

docs.title: Before merging a docs change
docs.text:
1. Ground every technical claim. A claim about behaviour, formulas or parameter effects must trace to a docstring, a science page or a test. A science page may name the function in an HTML comment:

    Markdown
    <!-- REFERENCE: per_capita_adjusted_budget() in src/fair_shares/library/allocations/budgets/per_capita.py -->

  2. Run every code example and check that its output and comments match the text.

  3. Build strictly: uv run mkdocs build --strict fails on broken links and missing pages. uv run mkdocs serve previews the site.
Change Update New parameter Docstring, docs/science/allocations.md if the maths changes, the how-to pages if users set it Bug fix Code, then the docstring if behaviour changed, then the examples it affects Clearer docs Read the docstring and science page first, and check your version against them

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
Pages in docs/ link to each other with relative paths to the .md file, for example [Allocation approaches](../science/allocations.md).

Code that links to the site builds the URL in one module, src/fair_shares/library/config/urls.py:

Name Purpose DOCS_BASE_URL Site root. Defaults to https://setupelz.github.io/fair-shares; FAIR_SHARES_DOCS_URL overrides it docs_url(path) Joins a page path to DOCS_BASE_URL. Drops a .md suffix and a leading slash, and adds a trailing slash DOCS_URLS Prebuilt URLs for common pages, grouped as science, user_guide and api Python
from fair_shares.library.config.urls import DOCS_URLS, docs_url

docs_url("science/allocations")
# "https://setupelz.github.io/fair-shares/science/allocations/"

DOCS_URLS["user_guide"]["approach_catalog"]

utils/io.py uses docs_url("user-guide/output-schema") to point output README files at the Outputs page. When the site moves, change DOCS_BASE_URL or set FAIR_SHARES_DOCS_URL, and every link built through docs_url follows. A page that renames a heading keeps the old anchor with {#old-anchor}, because docstrings and error messages link to anchors.

docs.title: Docstrings for allocation approaches
docs.text:
Docstrings follow the numpy convention and need four sections: a one-line summary, the mathematical foundation in LaTeX, every parameter, and the return value. The approaches in allocations/budgets/per_capita.py are the models.

Python
def my_new_allocation(
    population_ts: TimeseriesDataFrame,
    allocation_year: int,
    emission_category: str,
    group_level: str = "iso3c",
    unit_level: str = "unit",
    ur: pint.facets.PlainRegistry = get_default_unit_registry(),
) -> BudgetAllocationResult:
    r"""
    Short one-line summary of what this approach does.

    Longer description providing context on when to use this approach.

    Mathematical Foundation
    -----------------------

    The allocation is calculated as:

    $$
    A(g) = \frac{P(g, t_a)}{\sum_{g'} P(g', t_a)}
    $$

    Where:

    - $A(g)$: Budget share allocated to country $g$
    - $P(g, t_a)$: Population of country $g$ at allocation year $t_a$

    Parameters
    ----------
    population_ts
        Timeseries of population for each group
    allocation_year
        Year from which to start calculating allocations
    emission_category
        Emission category to include in the output
    group_level
        Level in the index which specifies group information
    unit_level
        Level in the index which specifies the unit of each timeseries
    ur
        The unit registry to use for calculations

    Returns
    -------
    BudgetAllocationResult
        Container with relative shares for cumulative emissions budget allocation.

    See Also
    --------
    `From Principle to Code <https://setupelz.github.io/fair-shares/science/principle-to-code/>`_
        Normative foundations and equity principles underlying allocation approaches.
    """
  • Use a raw string (r""") for LaTeX, and define every variable in an equation. Break a complex calculation into steps.
  • For key parameters, link to the matching section of the Parameter effects page. For adjustment weights, state the direction of the effect. Give valid ranges and defaults.
  • Check that the LaTeX renders with uv run mkdocs serve, and that parameter types match the signature.

docs.title: Reproductions
docs.text:
Each notebook in the 600 series reproduces one published study with the library. It extracts the study's method, maps each approach to library settings and runs it on the library's data. Run a notebook from the repository root, for example uv run python notebooks/602_reproduce_dekker_2025.py.

Notebook Study What it reproduces Accuracy 601_reproduce_esabcc_2023 ESABCC 2023; Pelz 2023 Equal per capita, equal cumulative per capita, responsibility and capability budgets for the EU27, from 1990 and 2015 EU27 shares within -0.41 to 0 pp for equal per capita and equal cumulative per capita. Responsibility differs by up to -1.76 pp, because the library allocates to countries and sums them (details) 602_reproduce_dekker_2025 Dekker 2025 Grandfathering, immediate per capita, per capita convergence, equal cumulative per capita, ability to pay and Greenhouse Development Rights pathways Expressed in library terms; input differences listed in the notebook 604_reproduce_vandenberg_2020 Van den Berg 2020 Grandfathering, immediate equal per capita, per capita convergence, equal cumulative per capita, ability to pay and Greenhouse Development Rights pathways, with a cost-optimal reference Expressed in library terms; input differences listed in the notebook 605_reproduce_matthews_2016 Matthews 2016; Gignac 2015 National carbon debts and the equal per capita budget allocation Expressed in library terms; input differences listed in the notebook

The studies use other emissions data, scopes and population vintages than the library defaults. Published numbers and library results therefore differ even where the method matches. Each notebook ends with a list of these differences.

The full citations are on the References page.

docs.title: ESABCC 2023 reproduction
docs.text:
The fair-share numbers in the ESABCC advice on the EU 2040 target (ESABCC 2023) come from an IIASA study, Pelz, Rogelj and Riahi (2023), here PRR2023 (report, replication code). Notebook 601_reproduce_esabcc_2023 runs the same approaches with the library and current data.

In short:

  • Notebook 601 uses the PRR2023 settings through a preset, esabcc_2023_allocations(). The library defaults differ.
  • The global budget is smaller than in PRR2023: 1331 Gt from 1990 (PRR2023: 1530 Gt) and 651 Gt from 2015 (PRR2023: 704 Gt). Two choices cause most of this: the years before 2020 are added as fossil CO2 only, and international aviation and shipping are deducted.
  • The EU27 shares match PRR2023 closely; see Reproduction accuracy.
  • Notebook 601 also extends PRR2023 to land-use CO2 and the other greenhouse gases, and to budgets remaining from today.

The details follow in the boxes below. Remaining carbon budgets, Scenario sets and Greenhouse gases explain the budget corrections, the scenario sets and the gas treatment for every run.

What PRR2023 computed Element PRR2023 Emissions in scope Fossil and industry CO2 (co2-ffi) Global budget IPCC AR6 WGI, 1.5°C at 50%: 500 Gt CO2 from 2020 Allocation years 1990 and 2015. The year 1850 enters only as the start of a responsibility window Budget from the allocation year 1530 Gt from 1990 and 704 Gt from 2015: 500 Gt plus 1030 Gt and 204 Gt from Global Carbon Budget 2021 (Friedlingstein 2022) National emissions Global Carbon Budget 2022, national fossil emissions Approaches Equal per capita (EPC), equal cumulative per capita (ECPC), responsibility, capability. The responsibility-capability-need composite stays unquantified Responsibility windows Fossil CO2 1850 to 1989 (allocation year 1990); 1850 to 2014 and 1990 to 2014 (allocation year 2015); total and per capita Capability GDP per capita in 1990 or 2014 Penalty functions 1/x and 1/√x Spatial unit 11 world regions plus EU27 Settings in notebook 601 and the preset PRR2023 approach fair-shares approach Settings EPC equal-per-capita-budget allocation_year 1990 or 2015, preserve_allocation_year_shares=True ECPC equal-per-capita-budget allocation_year 1990 or 2015, preserve_allocation_year_shares=False, cumulative_end_year=2050 Responsibility per-capita-adjusted-budget functional form "power", exponent 1.0 (1/x) or 0.5 (1/√x), window start 1850 or 1990, total or per capita, on both bases Capability per-capita-adjusted-budget functional form "power", exponent 1.0 or 0.5, capability_reference_year 1990 (allocation year 1990) or 2014 (allocation year 2015), on both bases

The library defaults differ: functional form "asinh", no 2050 population window, GDP year by year. A tool that presents the PRR2023 approaches takes its settings from the preset (Presets):

Python
from fair_shares.library.presets import esabcc_2023_allocations

allocations = esabcc_2023_allocations("co2-ffi")  # the PRR2023 matrix, 36 runs

Notebook 601 uses one budget, ar6_2020 at 1.5°C and 50%. Its section 5 subtracts observed emissions and reports the budget remaining from 2026 (from 2025 for all-ghg, whose land-use data end in 2024). Its section 6 spreads each remaining budget into an annual pathway to 2100.

Differences from PRR2023 and their effect Topic PRR2023 Notebook 601 Effect National emissions GCB 2022 PRIMAP-hist v2.8, the library default (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) Changes responsibility indicators Budget from 1990 and 2015 Adds total CO2 for 1990 to 2019 (1030 Gt) and 2015 to 2019 (204 Gt) Adds fossil CO2 without bunkers: 857 Gt and 177 Gt 1331 Gt from 1990 and 651 Gt from 2015, about 13% and 7% below PRR2023. Every national budget falls by the same proportion International aviation and shipping Inside the 500 Gt Deducted, 2020 to net zero: 26 Gt, so 500 Gt becomes 474 Gt Lowers every national budget Future land-use CO2 Not separated Median of the AR6 C1 scenarios, a net sink, set to 0 by the precautionary cap No effect at 1.5°C Population WiC SSP2 (2013), OWID history UN WPP 2024 with UN and OWID history Changes ECPC shares GDP WDI PPP, constant 2017 dollars Same indicator, rebased to constant 2021 dollars Changes capability shares Spatial unit 11 regions plus EU27 177 countries plus rest of world Changes responsibility and capability shares (see the check below) Consumption CO2, capital stock Used No data source Indicators absent

docs.title: Reproduction accuracy
docs.text:
Notebook 601 reproduces PRR2023 closely. The table compares the EU27 share of the global budget, in per cent.

Approach PRR2023 fair-shares Difference (pp) Equal per capita, from 1990 7.88 7.88 +0.01 Equal per capita, from 2015 5.96 5.94 -0.02 Equal cumulative per capita, from 1990 5.93 5.65 -0.28 Equal cumulative per capita, from 2015 5.47 5.06 -0.41 Capability, all variants -0.36 to +0.04 Responsibility, all variants -1.77 to +0.31

The cumulative per capita rows differ through the newer population projections. The responsibility rows differ most because fair-shares allocates to countries and sums them, while PRR2023 allocates to the EU27 as one region. With the same regional inputs, the library reproduces the PRR2023 results exactly.

Extensions beyond PRR2023: land-use CO2 and other gases

Notebook 601 also runs co2 (with land-use CO2 as national inventories report it), all-ghg-ex-co2-lulucf and all-ghg. A remaining carbon budget limits CO2 only, so the CO2 part is a budget and the non-CO2 part is an annual pathway; the library holds no single greenhouse-gas budget number. At 1.5°C and 50% the co2 budget from 2020 is 383 Gt (474 Gt minus a 91 Gt national-inventory convention gap). The all-GHG categories start in 2015 in notebook 601; all-ghg cannot start before 2000, the first year of national-inventory land-use data. Greenhouse gases explains the method and the sources behind it.

The sources cited here are on the References page.

docs.title: Method overview
docs.text:
fair-shares computes fair shares of a global emissions limit, for countries or for the regions of an integrated assessment model (IAM). The limit is a global remaining carbon budget or a global emissions pathway. The result is one cumulative budget per country or region, or a value for every year.

This page walks the full chain in five steps, with countries as the example. Each step names its sources and links to the page with the detail.

In short:

  • The starting point is a published global remaining carbon budget.
  • fair-shares adjusts that budget so that it matches what countries report in their national inventories (Weber 2026).
  • Equity-based allocation approaches split the adjusted budget among countries, either as one cumulative budget or year by year along a global pathway (Pelz 2025a; Pelz 2025b).
  • CO₂ is allocated as a budget and the other greenhouse gases as an annual pathway from scenarios at the same warming level (Weber 2026b).
  • Observed emissions to date give each country's remaining budget, which can be spread into an annual pathway.

docs.title: 1. Published global budget
docs.text:
A remaining carbon budget is the net CO₂ the world can still emit until CO₂ reaches net zero, for a warming level and a likelihood. The library ships budgets from five sources, for example 500 Gt CO₂ from 2020 for 1.5 °C at 50% in IPCC AR6. Each budget limits CO₂ only.

Sources: IPCC 2021 SPM; Lamboll 2023; Forster 2024; Forster 2026. Detail: Published budgets, What a budget label means.

docs.title: 2. Allocatable budget
docs.text:
Every budget is rebased to start in 2020 with observed emissions. International aviation and shipping leave the budget because national inventories report them only as memo items outside their national totals. For fossil CO₂ the projected land-use share leaves the budget. For total CO₂ land use switches to the national-inventory convention, which lowers the budget.

Sources: Weber 2026; scenarios from Gidden 2023. Detail: Remaining carbon budgets, Scenario sets.

docs.title: 3. Allocation approaches
docs.text:
An allocation approach turns an equity principle into each country's share of a global limit. The approaches start from equal per capita shares and can adjust them for historical responsibility, capability and inequality within countries. Each approach comes in two forms:

  • A budget approach divides a global budget and gives one cumulative value per country.
  • A pathway approach divides a global pathway year by year and gives annual values. The pathway is a scenario pathway, such as one from IPCC AR6, or a budget turned into a pathway.

The same approaches also divide among IAM model regions. The region route reads population, GDP and emissions from the scenario file. The IAM's own Emissions|Covered then sets the global limit and the budget adjustments of step 2 therefore apply only to the country route.

Sources: Pelz 2025a; Pelz 2025b. Detail: Allocation approaches, From principle to code, Parameter effects, RCB pathway generation, IAM model regions.

docs.title: 4. Greenhouse gases
docs.text:
Four categories are available: co2-ffi, co2, all-ghg-ex-co2-lulucf and all-ghg. A carbon budget limits CO₂ only, so an all-GHG result is a CO₂ budget plus a non-CO₂ annual pathway, both allocated with the same equity approach. The non-CO₂ pathway comes from scenarios at the budget's warming level, because the budget depends on the methane pathway it assumes.

Sources: Weber 2026b; Weber 2026 for land-use CO₂. Detail: Greenhouse gases.

docs.title: 5. Remaining budgets and pathways
docs.text:
A country's remaining budget is its allocation minus its observed emissions from the allocation year to the last observed year. A remaining budget can be negative when past emissions exceed the allocation. An annual pathway to an end year such as 2100 spreads it: each country moves from its current share towards an equal per capita share, and a deviation term makes the pathway sum to its remaining budget.

Detail: Past non-CO₂ use, Python API, RCB pathway generation.
