docs.title: Remaining carbon budgets
docs.text:
A remaining carbon budget is the net CO₂ the world can still emit from a start year until CO₂ reaches net zero. Each budget holds warming to a stated level with a stated likelihood. fair-shares takes a published budget and adjusts it to match what countries report in their national inventories. The adjustments follow Weber 2026.

In short:

  • The library ships budgets from IPCC AR6 WGI, Lamboll et al. (2023) and the Indicators of Global Climate Change updates (Forster et al. 2024 and 2026).
  • Every budget is rebased to start in 2020 with observed emissions.
  • International aviation and shipping (bunkers) are deducted because national inventories report them only as memo items outside their national totals.
  • For fossil CO₂ (co2-ffi), the land-use share of the budget is removed. A projected land sink never adds to the fossil budget.
  • For total CO₂ (co2), land-use CO₂ switches to the national-inventory convention. This lowers the budget.

docs.text:
data/rcbs/rcbs.yaml holds five sources. All values are in Gt CO₂ of total anthropogenic CO₂: fossil, bunkers and land use. A budget from the start of year \(X\) has baseline_year: X.

docs.title: From published budget to allocatable budget
docs.text:
A published budget counts total CO₂ from its own baseline year. Its land-use CO₂ follows the bookkeeping-model (BM) convention. National inventories count land use differently and leave out bunkers. Three adjustments close these gaps:

  1. Rebase to 2020. Observed emissions fill the years from 2020 to the baseline year.
  2. Bunker deduction. Bunker CO₂ from 2020 to net zero leaves the budget.
  3. Land-use term. For co2-ffi, the land-use share of the budget leaves the budget. For co2, land-use CO₂ switches from the BM convention to the national-inventory (NGHGI) convention.
Equations Symbol Definition \(\text{RCB}_{\text{BM}}(\text{base})\) Published budget from the baseline year, in BM convention \(F_{\text{actual}}(a, b)\) Cumulative observed fossil CO₂ without international bunkers, years \(a\) to \(b\) (e.g. PRIMAP) \(L_{\text{BM}}(a, b)\) Cumulative BM land-use CO₂ from the scenario median (AFOLU|Direct), years \(a\) to \(b\) \(L_{\text{NGHGI}}(a, b)\) Cumulative observed NGHGI land-use CO₂ (world row of the LULUCF source, Melo et al.), years \(a\) to \(b\) \(B(a, b)\) Cumulative international bunker CO₂, years \(a\) to \(b\) \(\text{gap}(a, b)\) Cumulative NGHGI minus BM convention gap for CO₂, years \(a\) to \(b\) \(\text{NZ}\) Net-zero year (from scenario data) \(\text{base}\) Baseline year of the budget (e.g. 2023 for Lamboll, 2020 for AR6 WGI)

Fossil-only budget (co2-ffi):

\[ \mathrm{fossil{\_}budget}(2020) = \text{RCB}_{\text{BM}}(\text{base}) + F_{\text{actual}}(2020,\, \text{base}{-}1) + B(2020,\, \text{base}{-}1) - L_{\text{BM}}(\text{base},\, \text{NZ}) - B(2020,\, \text{NZ}) \]

Total CO₂ budget (co2):

\[ \mathrm{nghgi{\_}budget}(2020) = \text{RCB}_{\text{BM}}(\text{base}) + F_{\text{actual}}(2020,\, \text{base}{-}1) + B(2020,\, \text{base}{-}1) + L_{\text{NGHGI}}(2020,\, \text{base}{-}1) + \text{gap}(\text{base},\, \text{NZ}) - B(2020,\, \text{NZ}) \]

with \(\text{gap}(a, b) = \int_{a}^{b} \left[L_{\text{NGHGI}}(t) - L_{\text{BM}}(t)\right] dt\).

The co2 case has no land-use decomposition. Its land use stays in the budget and changes convention.

Which data feed each term

The past uses observed data. Scenario data enter only for future quantities.

Term Data Coverage Fossil rebase (\(F_{\text{actual}}\)) PRIMAP-hist v2.8 (primap-202609, default), v2.6.1 (primap-202503) or GCB 2025 (gcb-2025, co2-ffi only) 1850 to 2025 (v2.8); 1850 to 2023 (v2.6.1); 1850 to 2024 (GCB) Bunker rebase and observed bunkers (\(B\)) GCB 2025 (gcb-2025) to 2024 NGHGI land-use rebase (\(L_{\text{NGHGI}}\), co2 only) Melo et al. (2026) world row: v4.0.0 (melo-2026-v4, default) or v3.1.1 (melo-2026) 2000 to 2024, 187 countries (v4.0.0); 2000 to 2023, 185 countries (v3.1.1) BM land-use term (\(L_{\text{BM}}\), co2-ffi only) Gidden et al. AR6 reanalysis, scenario median of AFOLU|Direct 2015 to 2100 Convention gap (co2 only) Observed NGHGI, then AFOLU|Indirect from the same reanalysis 2015 to 2100 Net-zero crossing (NZ) The same reanalysis, Emissions|CO2 Interpolated per scenario Future bunkers A bunker share of the set's median net CO₂ (AR6, Scenario Compass and ScenarioMIP scenarios that report bunkers) From 2025 to net zero Budget from 2020 Global Carbon Budget 2025 global workbook (gcb-2025-global) 1959 to 2024; 2025 takes the 2024 value

docs.title: Rebase to 2020
docs.text:
The rebase moves the start of every budget to 2020. A budget published from a later year gets back the observed emissions of 2020 to the year before its baseline:

  • Fossil CO₂. The world fossil series leaves out international bunkers. The PRIMAP world total equals the sum of its countries. The gcb-2025 world row is the GCB global total minus bunkers.
  • Bunkers. The published budget holds bunkers, and the fossil series does not. The output column is rebase_bunkers_mt.
  • Land-use CO₂ (co2 only). Observed land-use CO₂ in the NGHGI convention, from the world row of the active LULUCF source (Melo et al.), which notebook 107 writes. The output column is rebase_lulucf_mt.

For a budget from 2020 every rebase term is zero.

Why the co2-ffi rebase adds no land-use CO₂

The published budget is in the BM convention, so a full rebase would add BM land-use CO₂ for 2020 to \(\text{base}{-}1\). The decomposition would then remove BM land-use CO₂ for 2020 to NZ:

\[ L_{\text{BM}}(2020,\, \text{base}{-}1) - L_{\text{BM}}(2020,\, \text{NZ}) = -L_{\text{BM}}(\text{base},\, \text{NZ}) \]

The years 2020 to \(\text{base}{-}1\) cancel. The formula therefore omits land use from the rebase and starts the decomposition at \(\text{base}\). This form suits the pipeline because it needs no observed land-use series in the BM convention.

Why the co2 rebase adds NGHGI land-use CO₂

The target quantity is cumulative fossil CO₂ plus NGHGI land-use CO₂ from 2020 to NZ. The published budget holds fossil CO₂, bunkers and BM land-use CO₂ from \(\text{base}\) to NZ.

For 2020 to \(\text{base}{-}1\) the rebase adds the observed quantities in the target convention: fossil CO₂, bunkers and NGHGI land-use CO₂. For \(\text{base}\) to NZ the convention gap converts the land-use share of the published budget from BM to NGHGI. Each year from 2020 to NZ is converted once.

Years without observed data

The rebase needs a value for every year from 2020 to \(\text{base}{-}1\) in each series it adds. When a series ends earlier, each later year takes its last observed value, with a warning that names the source, series, years and value. This fill is a placeholder until observed data are published. rebase_fill_max_years in rcbs.yaml caps the filled years per series (default 1; 0 turns the fill off). A source that needs more is left out of the processed budgets, with one warning listing it.

Budget Emissions or land-use source Fill forster_2026 (baseline 2026) primap-202609 (to 2025) none forster_2026 gcb-2025 emissions and bunkers (to 2024) 2025 takes the 2024 value forster_2026 primap-202503 (to 2023) two years missing: left out forster_2026, co2 melo-2026-v4 (to 2024) 2025 takes the 2024 value forster_2026, co2 melo-2026 (to 2023) two years missing: left out lamboll_2023, forster_2024 any none

After the last observed year the bunker deduction uses the bunker share, while a filled rebase year holds the last observed value. The two can count that year differently: 2025 for forster_2026 with gcb-2025 bunkers.

docs.title: Bunker deduction
docs.text:
International aviation and shipping count towards global emission totals but national inventories report them only as memo items outside their national totals. The deduction removes them from 2020 to net zero, for every baseline year.

Observed bunkers count from 2020 to the last observed year \(L\) (gcb-2025 by default, \(L = 2024\)). After \(L\), bunkers are a share \(s\) of the median net CO₂ of the budget's scenario set. The share comes from every scenario that reports bunkers, balanced across model families (Bunker share). With the default sources \(s = 0.072\). The 1.5 °C (50%) budgets thus deduct 4.96 Gt of observed bunkers (2020 to 2024) plus 0.072 times 225 to 293 Gt of set net CO₂. A set with more net CO₂ after \(L\) takes more bunkers.

Equation and why the rebase adds bunkers \[ B(2020,\, \text{NZ}) = \sum_{t=2020}^{L} B_{\text{obs}}(t) + s \cdot \underset{i \in \text{set}}{\text{median}}\; C_i(L{+}1,\, t_{\text{nz},i}) \]

\(C_i\) is the cumulative net CO₂ of scenario \(i\) of the budget's volume-matched set (or AR6 category) from the start of \(L{+}1\) to its net-zero crossing.

The two bunker terms count each bunker year once. The bunker rebase restores the published budget to a total-CO₂ budget from 2020. The deduction then removes every bunker year from 2020 to NZ:

\[ B(2020,\, \text{base}{-}1) - B(2020,\, \text{NZ}) = -B(\text{base},\, \text{NZ}) \]

The years 2020 to \(\text{base}{-}1\) cancel, and the net deduction covers the years that the published budget holds. The result is the budget from 2020 without any bunker emissions, for every baseline year.

The function is bunker_deduction_from_share() in src/fair_shares/library/utils/data/nghgi.py.

docs.title: Land-use term for fossil CO₂
docs.text:
A published budget includes land-use CO₂. A fossil-only budget removes the land-use share from the baseline year to net zero. No observation covers these future years, so the term comes from scenarios. Each scenario of the budget's volume-matched set (Role-matched scenario sets) gives its cumulative AFOLU|Direct flux from the baseline year to its own net-zero crossing. The term is the median across these scenarios. Notebook 104 stores one median per baseline year as bm_lulucf_median_from in rcb_scenario_adjustments.yaml.

A precautionary cap (default on) keeps a projected land sink from adding to the fossil budget. A net land source still reduces it. The sink relies on uncertain future reforestation, so the cap sets a net sink to zero. precautionary_lulucf: false in the adjustments config turns the cap off for sensitivity analysis.

Equation \[ L_{\text{BM}}^{\text{capped}} = \max\!\left(0,\; \underset{i}{\text{median}}\int_{\text{base}}^{t_{\text{nz},i}} L_{\text{BM},i}(t)\,dt\right) \]

The structure follows Weber 2026 (Methods, Eqs. 2 and 3). Differences from Weber et al. (2026) lists where the package departs from it.

rcb_scenario_adjustments.yaml also holds convention_gap_median_from for every budget. Only co2 allocations read it.

docs.title: National-inventory convention gap for total CO₂
docs.text:
Bookkeeping models (e.g. BLUE, OSCAR) estimate only direct human-caused land-use fluxes: deforestation, afforestation and land management. National inventories (NGHGIs) also count indirect effects, such as CO₂ fertilisation of managed forests and climate-driven changes in soil carbon. NGHGI land-use CO₂ is therefore a larger net sink than the BM estimate. The global difference is 5 to 7 Gt CO₂ per year, mainly from CO₂ fertilisation on managed land (Weber 2026).

A total CO₂ budget keeps land use and switches it to the NGHGI convention. The convention gap covers the years of the published budget, from the baseline year to net zero. Weber 2026 (Methods, Eqs. 2 and 3) uses the same split: the correction starts at the reference year of the budget, and earlier years take observed NGHGI land-use CO₂. The gap is negative, so it reduces the allocatable budget. Notebook 104 stores one median per baseline year in convention_gap_median_from. The output column is correction_lulucf_convention_mt.

How the gap is computed per scenario

The per-scenario gap \(\text{Gap}_i\) runs from the baseline year \(\text{base}\) to the net-zero crossing of the scenario. It has two segments.

Observed (\(\text{base} \leq t \leq \mathrm{splice{\_}year}\)): observed NGHGI land-use CO₂ (the same for all scenarios) minus the BM flux of scenario \(i\). The splice year is the last year of the NGHGI data (2023 for melo-2026, 2024 for melo-2026-v4). NGHGI data come from Melo et al. and the BM flux from the Gidden et al. AR6 reanalysis (AFOLU|Direct). Other sources of the same quantities can take these roles.

\[ \text{Gap}_{i,\text{obs}} = \int_{\text{base}}^{\min(\text{splice},\, t_{\text{nz},i})} \left[\text{NGHGI}_{\text{actual}}(t) - \text{BM}_{\text{Direct},i}(t)\right] dt \]

Future (\(t > \mathrm{splice{\_}year}\)): only the indirect component of scenario \(i\) (CO₂ fertilisation and other passive fluxes), because the direct components cancel. It comes from the Gidden et al. AR6 reanalysis (AFOLU|Indirect).

\[ \text{Gap}_{i,\text{future}} = \int_{\max(\text{base},\, \text{splice})}^{t_{\text{nz},i}} \text{Indirect}_{i}(t)\, dt \]

The total is \(\text{Gap}_i = \text{Gap}_{i,\text{obs}} + \text{Gap}_{i,\text{future}}\). The median runs over the volume-matched set or the AR6 category of the budget, and a budget takes the median of its own baseline year. Each year counts in full, and the net-zero year adds its fraction (Full-year accounting).

Edge cases:

  • A baseline year after the splice year leaves the observed segment empty. The gap is then the indirect component from \(\text{base}\).
  • A scenario that reaches net zero before \(\text{base}\) has a gap of zero.
  • The years 2020 to \(\text{base}{-}1\) sit outside the gap. The rebase adds observed NGHGI land-use CO₂ for them.

The per-scenario function is convention_gap_from_baseline() in src/fair_shares/library/utils/data/rcb.py.

docs.title: Differences from Weber et al. (2026)
docs.text:
The package follows the structure of Weber 2026 (Methods, Eqs. 2 and 3), with five differences.

The five differences
  1. Scenario sets. Weber et al. use AR6 C1 scenarios for 1.5 °C (50%) and C3 for 2 °C (66%). The package uses these categories for the AR6 sources and role-matched sets for the other sources.
  2. Statistic. Weber et al. take the mean across scenarios for the land-use and bunker terms. The package takes the median.
  3. BM side. Weber et al. adjust the Gidden et al. values with the difference between the Global Carbon Budget mean of bookkeeping models and NGHGI-reported values for 2020 to 2023 (Methods, "Calculating a NGHGI-consistent global RCB"). The package uses the scenario AFOLU|Direct flux, also for the observed years from the baseline year to the splice year, and holds no observed BM series. The gap is a per-scenario quantity: each scenario has its own AFOLU|Direct pathway, net-zero year and indirect flux. One multi-model average would collapse this variation and break the integrate-then-median method.
  4. Bunker term. Weber et al. take the bunker pathways of the C1 or C3 scenarios that report aviation and maritime (8 and 9 scenarios). The package applies a family-balanced bunker share of net CO₂ to the scenario set of every budget, AR6 categories included.
  5. Accounting. The package counts full years to an interpolated net-zero crossing for every term.

docs.title: Allocation years other than 2020
docs.text:
The allocatable budget runs from 2020. The allocation_year parameter moves the start. An earlier year adds the world's historical emissions before 2020. A later year subtracts the emissions already used.

The world series matches the adjusted budget. It holds fossil CO₂ without bunkers and, for total CO₂, NGHGI land-use CO₂:

\[ E_{\text{world}}(t) = E_{\text{fossil}}(t) + \text{LULUCF}(t) \]

NGHGI land-use data start in 2000: LULUCF Data Hub v4.0.0 (melo-2026-v4, default, 2000 to 2024) or v3.1.1 (melo-2026, opt-in, 2000 to 2023). Categories with land-use CO₂ therefore start in 2000 or later (Start-year limits). An allocation year before the first year of the world series raises an error that names the first available year. calculate_budget_from_rcb then works the same way for co2-ffi and co2. build_world_co2_timeseries() and the preprocessing notebooks build the same series.

Why land-use CO₂ starts in 2000

The official NGHGI land-use data begin in 2000. Earlier NGHGI estimates exist, such as historical extensions of Melo et al. Extending to 1990 would splice heterogeneous datasets, and the BM-to-NGHGI transition around 1990 shows a large jump. The package performs no NGHGI/BM splicing. We plan to extend coverage when validated pre-2000 NGHGI land-use data become available.

docs.title: Budgets outside the defaults
docs.text:
Some published labels stay out of the default rcbs.yaml, because their scenario sets are too thin:

  • 1.5 °C budgets with high likelihoods (forster_2024, forster_2026, ar6_wg1_2021). Fewer than 10 volume-matched scenarios.

To run one, add its label and published value to data/rcbs/rcbs.yaml. Each of its scenario sets must hold at least min_scenarios scenarios.

docs.text:
The two boxes trace one budget from 2020 and one from 2023 through every adjustment, with values from pipeline runs on the default sources.

A budget from 2020: IPCC AR6 WGI, 1.5 °C at 50%

IPCC AR6 WGI, 1.5 °C at 50% (ar6_2020, 1.5p50): 500 Gt CO₂ from 2020. It takes AR6 category C1: 70 scenarios, all reaching net zero. Values come from pipeline runs on the default sources: PRIMAP-hist v2.8 (primap-202609), LULUCF Data Hub v4.0.0 (melo-2026-v4) and gcb-2025 bunkers. Each row is rounded, and the totals use unrounded values.

Runs behind the numbers

The co2-ffi values come from a budget run of co2-ffi on the default sources, with PRIMAP-hist v2.8 emissions. The co2 values come from a budget run of all-ghg on the same sources, with land-use CO₂ from the LULUCF Data Hub (melo-2026-v4).

docs.title: Scenario sets
docs.text:
Some budget terms need future emissions: the land-use term, the convention gap, the bunker deduction after the last observation and the non-CO₂ pathway. fair-shares takes these from published scenarios. This page explains how it reads a budget label and picks the scenarios for each term. Remaining carbon budgets explains the terms themselves.

In short:

  • A budget label names the warming when CO₂ reaches net zero and a likelihood. What the likelihood covers depends on the source.
  • Each scenario-derived term takes the set that matches its role: a volume-matched set for land use, the convention gap and bunkers, and a temperature-matched set for the non-CO₂ pathway.
  • The AR6 budgets take the matching AR6 category (C1, C3 or C4) for every term.
  • The bunker share pools every scenario that reports bunkers, balanced across model families.
  • Every cumulative counts full years to an interpolated net-zero crossing.

docs.title: What a budget label means
docs.text:
A label TpL names a warming level \(T\) and a likelihood \(L\). Each budget runs from its start year to net-zero CO₂. \(T\) is the warming when CO₂ reaches net zero. It equals peak warming when the zero-emissions commitment (ZEC) is zero. Lamboll 2023 defines \(T\) as peak warming.

The likelihood of AR6 WGI and of the IGCC updates covers the uncertainty of the transient climate response to cumulative emissions (TCRE) only. The likelihood of Lamboll et al. covers TCRE, ZEC and Earth-system feedbacks (ESF). Every published budget assumes the median non-CO₂ warming of scenarios at \(T\), for every likelihood.

Source key Likelihood covers \(T\) measures ar6_2020 TCRE only Warming at net zero ar6_wg1_2021 TCRE only Warming at net zero lamboll_2023 TCRE, ZEC, ESF Peak warming forster_2024 TCRE only Warming at net zero forster_2026 TCRE only Warming at net zero

Each source records likelihood_scope and budget_metric in rcbs.yaml, and the processed budget files carry both.

forster_2024 and ar6_2020 publish 67% budgets under the label 2p67. The label 2p66 reads as 2p67 for these two sources, with a deprecation warning. Lamboll et al. publish 66%, so lamboll_2023 keeps 2p66.

docs.title: Role-matched scenario sets
docs.text:
Each scenario-derived term of a budget takes the scenario set that matches its role. This is the default rule, scenario_selection: role-matched.

Term Set Rule Why Land-use term (co2-ffi) Volume-matched Reaches net-zero CO₂ by 2100; cumulative net CO₂ from 2020 to net zero within ±volume_tolerance_gt (50 Gt) of the budget from 2020 The term integrates to net zero, so its scenarios spend the budget's volume Convention gap (co2) Volume-matched Same Same Bunkers after the last observed year Volume-matched, times the bunker share Median net CO₂ of the set from the year after the last observed year to net zero, times the share \(s\) Few scenarios report bunkers and \(s\) therefore pools every scenario that does (Bunker share) Non-CO₂ pathway Temperature-matched Net-zero year; median warming at net zero in \([T - 0.05,\; T + 0.05)\), for every likelihood Published budgets assume the median non-CO₂ warming at \(T\)

Every set needs a net-zero year, in the AR6 convention (Net zero).

A set below min_scenarios (10) raises a ConfigurationError that names the budget. The settings sit at the top of rcbs.yaml. The selection logic is in src/fair_shares/library/utils/data/scenario_sets.py.

docs.title: Budget from 2020
docs.text:
The volume-matched set compares each scenario with the budget from the start of 2020. That is the published value plus observed global net CO₂ from 2020 to the year before the baseline. Observed net CO₂ is fossil CO₂ (including bunkers) minus the cement carbonation sink plus bookkeeping land-use CO₂. It comes from the Global Carbon Budget 2025 workbook (gcb-2025-global, GCP 2026). The workbook ends in 2024, so forster_2026 takes the 2024 value for 2025 (rebase_fill_max_years).

Consistency record

rcb_scenario_adjustments.yaml records per budget:

  • the label as published, the likelihood scope and the metric;
  • the rule and size of each set, its median cumulative CO₂, and its median and 67th-percentile warming at net zero;
  • a check of the two sets: their overlap and the volume gap of the temperature-matched set (its median cumulative CO₂ minus the budget from 2020).

For a p50 budget the two sets describe one budget, so a small gap supports the pairing.

docs.title: AR6 category pools
docs.text:
ar6_2020 and ar6_wg1_2021 set scenario_selection: ar6-category. Their labels with an AR6 WGIII category take that category for every term: 1.5p50 C1, 2p67 C3, 2p50 C4.

  • C1 limits warming to 1.5 °C (>50%) with no or limited overshoot.
  • C3 limits warming to 2 °C (>67%).
  • C4 limits warming to 2 °C (>50%).

These definitions come from IPCC 2022 Annex III, Table 14. C2 returns warming to 1.5 °C (>50%) by 2100 after a high overshoot. Its warming peaks above 1.5 °C and a budget counts emissions to peak warming, so C2 stays outside every budget label. The integral terms use the category members that reach net zero. The non-CO₂ pathway uses every member. The bunker term applies the same bunker share to the net CO₂ of the category set. The other labels of these sources use the role-matched sets.

docs.title: Net zero
docs.text:
A scenario reaches net-zero CO₂ in the first full year from 2020 at which its harmonised climate-assessment CO₂, linear between reported years, is at or below zero. A scenario without such a year still counts when its harmonised or reported CO₂ falls below 100 Mt CO₂/yr by 2100. Its net-zero year is the first such year. This is the count of AR6 WGIII: "Pathways were counted when at least one of the two profiles fell below 100 MtCO2 yr–1 until 2100" (IPCC 2022 SPM, Table SPM.2, note j). net_zero_years() in src/fair_shares/library/utils/data/scenario_sources.py applies the rule.

The AR6 metadata give a net-zero year to the same 591 of the 914 AR6 scenarios. For 72 of them, which reach net zero only under the 100 Mt rule, the AR6 warming at net zero holds the 2100 value. fair-shares therefore derives the net-zero year and the warming at net zero of every AR6 scenario from the AR6 Scenarios Database series (ipcc_ar6_climate). On the other 519 scenarios the derived warming matches the AR6 metadata within 0.013 °C.

docs.title: Scenario sets of the default budgets
docs.text:
Two readings follow from the sets of the default budgets:

  • The volume-matched sets of 1.5 and 1.7 °C p67 budgets have a 67th-percentile warming at net zero 0.08 to 0.18 °C above \(T\); for p83 and p90 budgets at 1.7 °C the difference is 0.00 to 0.02 °C. For 2 °C p66 and p67 the difference is within 0.02 °C. The budget likelihood covers TCRE only, and the MAGICC percentile covers more uncertainty.
  • The AR6 budgets use the AR6 category pools, whose scenarios spend less than the budget to net zero: the C4 median is 1153 Gt against 1350 Gt (2p50), and the C3 median 834 Gt against 1150 Gt (2p67).
Set statistics per default budget

Counts from the AR6 reanalysis of Gidden et al. (2023), 914 scenarios. Budgets from 2020 and set statistics in Gt CO₂. Warming is MAGICCv7.5.3 at net zero.

The adjustments file of every run holds the rows of the other labels. Budgets outside the defaults lists the labels left out and why.

docs.title: Bunker share
docs.text:
Few scenarios report international aviation and shipping. The bunker term therefore uses one share \(s\) of net CO₂, taken from every scenario that reports bunkers. Bunker deduction shows how the budget applies it.

Each scenario that reports bunkers and reaches net zero gives a ratio \(r_k\): its cumulative bunkers over its own net CO₂ (the model's Emissions|CO2). Both run from the year after the last observed bunker year to the scenario's net-zero crossing. The share is family-balanced: the median of the per-family medians, \(s = \text{median}_f\, \text{median}_{k \in f}\, r_k\). A family counts only with at least bunkers.min_runs_per_family (3) scenarios. A family is the energy-model stem without version or coupling: IMAGE 3.2 and IMAGE 3.3 are IMAGE, and REMIND-MAgPIE 3.2-4.6 is REMIND.

With gcb-2025 bunkers (last observed year 2024) the share runs from 2025. The default pool is AR6, Scenario Compass v2.0 and ScenarioMIP v0.1. 156 scenarios that report bunkers reach net zero: 22 from AR6, 92 from Scenario Compass and 42 from ScenarioMIP.

Family Family median Scenarios Counts IMAGE 0.072 57 yes REMIND 0.071 46 yes MESSAGE 0.074 13 yes WITCH 0.051 12 yes GCAM 0.078 10 yes AIM 0.060 7 yes COFFEE 0.033 6 yes IMACLIM 0.106 5 yes GEM-E3 0.053 2 no McKinsey 0.097 2 no POLES 0.054 2 no LUT-ESTM 0.191 1 no

The family-balanced share is \(s = 0.072\). The median over all 156 scenarios is 0.072 (interquartile range 0.060 to 0.081). PROMETHEUS reports bunkers, and its runs end in 2050 without net zero.

Rules and checks
  • The scenarios come from every source in bunkers.scenario_sources (default [ar6, sci, scenariomip]). A run carried over from another listed source counts once: Scenario Compass flags its AR6 and ScenarioMIP runs.
  • Each scenario reaches net zero by its own net CO₂, in the AR6 convention (Net zero). The climate emulator behind a source therefore does not enter the share. ScenarioMIP uses MAGICC v7.6.0a3 and AR6 uses MAGICCv7.5.3.
  • No historical vetting applies to these scenarios. Vetting tests 2010 to 2025 totals, and the share needs the ratio within each model run.
  • model_families in src/fair_shares/conf/scenario_sources.yaml lists every model. A scenario from an unlisted model is a configuration error.
  • Fewer than bunkers.min_reporters (10) scenarios or bunkers.min_families (3) families, counted after the per-family filter, raise a ConfigurationError that names the count per scenario source.
  • A source whose data file is absent is left out with a warning.
  • Scenarios of both sources enter with their own emissions and the same accounting.
  • The record lists the excluded families with their medians and counts.

The function is bunker_share() in src/fair_shares/library/utils/data/scenario_sets.py.

Bunker series of each scenario source

AR6. The AR6 Scenarios Database (Byers 2022) has no bunker variable. It reports Emissions|CO2|Energy|Demand|Transportation|Aviation, which covers domestic and international flights, and ...|Transportation|Maritime. AR6 bunkers are 0.6 times aviation plus maritime. The factor 0.6 is the international share of aviation CO₂ that Weber 2026 takes from IEA data (58% to 62%). Maritime counts whole as international shipping, as in Weber et al. The series come from the public AR6 Scenarios Database (ipcc_ar6_bunkers). 39 of the 914 Gidden et al. scenarios report both variables for 2020 to 2100, all from IMAGE, and 22 of these reach net-zero CO₂ by 2100.

Scenario Compass. The ensemble reports Emissions|CO2|Energy|Demand|Bunkers and its international aviation and shipping parts directly, so it takes no aviation share. A scenario takes the total where reported, else the sum of both parts. Of the 1,977 scenarios of v2.0, 262 report bunkers with a net CO₂ series. 194 remain once the AR6 and ScenarioMIP runs count under their own source.

ScenarioMIP. The workbook reports bunkers like Scenario Compass. Its 68 model runs of 7 models all report them. The Ensemble envelope rows are left out.

docs.title: Scenario sources
docs.text: A scenario source is an entry in src/fair_shares/conf/scenario_sources.yaml.

docs.title: AR6 reanalysis
docs.text: The default source (ar6) is the reanalysis of the AR6 scenarios by Gidden et al. (2023), 914 scenarios (Gidden 2023). It supplies net CO₂, the land-use fluxes (AFOLU|Direct, AFOLU|Indirect), the non-CO₂ pathways, the net-zero years and the warming at net zero (MAGICCv7.5.3). The aviation and maritime series for the AR6 scenarios that report bunkers come from the AR6 Scenarios Database (Byers 2022).

docs.title: Scenario Compass
docs.text:
The Scenario Compass Initiative pathways ensemble (Huppmann 2026b, v2.0 of 8 October 2026; manuscript Riahi 2026) is the scenario source sci. Release v1.0 (Huppmann 2026) stays selectable through the version key, and each release names its own file and columns. Its terms and download are in Data & licences.

v2.0 holds 1,977 scenarios: the 1,214 AR6 carry-overs, the 68 ScenarioMIP v0.1 runs and later submissions. 524 scenarios pass the SCI 2025 historical vetting (criteria release v2026.08.03). The climate assessment comes in three workflows. fair-shares reads the AR6 workflow (MAGICC v7.5.3), the one behind the AR6 metadata. The metadata carry only peak warming and warming in 2100 and fair-shares therefore derives warming at net zero itself.

Warming at net zero for Scenario Compass and ScenarioMIP

Their metadata hold peak and 2100 warming only. warming_at_net_zero() takes the net-zero year of Net zero from the harmonised climate-assessment CO₂ and the model's reported CO₂. The warming at net zero is the median and 67th-percentile GSAT in that year. Without net zero by 2100, it is the 2100 warming. This follows the convention of the AR6 metadata. On the 914 AR6 scenarios that Scenario Compass carries over, it gives the same net-zero years as the AR6 series, and the AR6 metadata warming within 0.013 °C where the AR6 metadata hold the warming at net zero. A source without warming at net zero in its metadata declares a derived_warming block in scenario_sources.yaml.

non_co2.scenario_sources in rcbs.yaml (default [ar6]) lists the sources pooled into the temperature-matched non-CO₂ set. Scenario Compass adds its vetted scenarios that are not AR6 carry-overs: 84 in v2.0, of which 33 reach net zero. Their non-CO₂ is the harmonised-infilled Kyoto gases minus CO₂, harmonised to the historical non-CO₂. With a pooled source, the non-CO₂ pathway of a budget is the median of the per-scenario non-CO₂ over the set. The AR6 category budgets keep their AR6 category pool. The volume-matched land-use and convention-gap terms need the NGHGI reanalysis split, so they stay AR6 only.

docs.title: ScenarioMIP
docs.text:
ScenarioMIP-CMIP7 v0.1 (Riahi 2026b) holds 68 model runs of 7 models, with the climate assessment of MAGICC v7.6.0a3. It is the scenario source scenariomip, on by default for the bunker share and off for the non-CO₂ set. Its terms are in Data & licences.

Adding data sources lists what a new budget or scenario source needs.

docs.title: Scenario labels
docs.text:
Notebook 104 maps the categories of each scenario source to clean climate-assessment names and quantile fields. All downstream code, including the non-CO₂ pathways, then reads one format. AR6 categories map as:

  • C1 → climate-assessment="1.5C", quantile=0.5
  • C3 → climate-assessment="2C", quantile=0.67
  • C4 → climate-assessment="2C", quantile=0.5

C2 stays out of the map for the reason given in AR6 category pools. A new scenario source defines its own mapping into the same format. Inside notebook 104, combined labels (e.g. "1.5p50") keep C3 and C4 apart during the median step and map to the clean format at output. The map follows the AR6 WGIII category definitions (AR6 category pools).

docs.title: Full-year accounting
docs.text:
Budgets run from the start of 2020, so a cumulative counts every year in full. A scenario series is linear between its reported years, and the value of a year is its flow over that whole year. The net-zero year is the zero crossing of that line, interpolated between the last positive and the first non-positive point. A cumulative to net zero sums the full years from its start to the year before the crossing and adds the fraction of the crossing year (the trapezoid of the line within that year). The same accounting applies to the volume that selects the set, the land-use term, the convention gap and the bunker term. The functions are net_zero_crossing() and integrate() in src/fair_shares/library/utils/data/rcb.py.

Each scenario integrates to its own net-zero crossing \(t_{\text{nz},i}\), where its total CO₂ (Emissions|CO2) first reaches zero. This keeps negative emissions after net zero out of the corrections. Emissions|CO2 in IAM scenario databases is fossil plus BM land-use CO₂ by convention. This is a property of how scenarios report total CO₂. Every integral-term set holds only scenarios that reach net zero by 2100: the volume-matched set by its rule, and an AR6 category pool by keeping its members that reach net zero (192 of the 231 C3 scenarios).

Files written per budget

Notebook 104 keys each budget as source:label in rcb_scenario_adjustments.yaml, with the scalars and the consistency record. It also writes:

  • scenario_set_{source}_{label}.csv: the members of the integral-term set, with their net-zero crossings and net CO₂ from each possible start year;
  • bunker_share_reporters.csv: each scenario's cumulative bunkers and net CO₂ from every possible start year.

The processed budget files carry published_label, likelihood_scope, budget_metric, scenario_selection, budget_2020_gt, the rule and size of both sets and nz_year_median. They also carry the bunker columns: bunker_share, bunker_share_pooled, the interquartile range of the ratios, the family medians and counts (bunker_share_families), the scenario counts by source and the set's net CO₂ after the last observed year (bunker_set_co2_after_mt).

The sources cited here are on the References page.

docs.title: Which notebook do I start with?
docs.text:
Two questions decide it. What are you dividing up? A budget is one cumulative number per country. A pathway is a value for every year. Who between? Individual countries, or the model regions of an integrated assessment model.

Countries IAM model regions A budget 302_example_templates_budget_allocations run 400 once, then 402_example_iamc_budget_allocations A pathway 303_example_templates_pathway_allocations run 400 once, then 403_example_iamc_pathway_allocations Your own settings 301_custom_fair_share_allocation run 400 once, then 401_custom_iamc_allocation One region, model has no rest-of-world data 405_one_region_remaining_budget (One region of countries) Reproduce a published study 601 to 605 (see Reproductions)

The 302, 303, 402 and 403 notebooks run unchanged. You configure 301 and 401 yourself. 401 also exports a model-ready remaining budget.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
• Country fair shares: the country notebooks, step by step.
  • IAM model regions: preparing a scenario file with notebook 400 and allocating to its regions.
  • Updating data each year: moving to a new data release.
  • Reproduce a published study: the 600-series notebooks.
  • The ESABCC presets: national and EU27 budgets with the settings of the ESABCC 2023 advice.

Calling the library from your own Python code? See the Python API.

docs.title: Choosing an approach
docs.text:
Decide two things. First, do you need one cumulative number or a value for every year? Second, which principles count: equal entitlements, historical responsibility, capability, or a combination? From principle to code turns principles into settings. The Approach catalog lists every approach.

Every run records its parameters and data sources with the results (Outputs). Sources carry different licences (Data & licences).

docs.title: Approach catalog
docs.text: All allocation approaches at a glance. From principle to code maps principles to settings, and the API reference gives the maths.

docs.title: The Allocation Year Parameter
docs.text:
When allocation_year (budget) or first_allocation_year (pathway) is set in the past, the allocation considers cumulative population (and emissions, if using adjusted approaches) from that year onward when computing each country's share. The allocation itself is each country's share of the total budget from the allocation year. The library then subtracts each country's observed emissions from the allocation year to the last observed year, which gives its remaining budget. Notebook 601 and the Python API do this step (Remaining budgets and annual pathways).

The choice of start date is normatively significant: 1850 captures the full industrial era, 1950 tracks post-war growth, and 1990 corresponds to the IPCC First Assessment Report, widely treated in the equity literature as the "excusable ignorance" threshold, beyond which responsibility for emissions harm is difficult to deny Baer 2013; Pelz 2025b. For the philosophical origin of the excusable-ignorance defence and its rebuttal, see Shue 2015 and Caney 2010.

See Allocation Approaches for configuration details.

docs.title: Budget Approaches
docs.text:
Allocate a cumulative emissions budget at a single point in time.

Approach Use Case equal-per-capita-budget Population-proportional targets per-capita-adjusted-budget Additional weighting by pre-allocation responsibility (historical emissions) and capability (GDP) per-capita-adjusted-gini-budget Accounts for within-country inequality

docs.title: Pathway Approaches
docs.text: Allocate emissions over multiple years, producing annual shares.

docs.title: Equal Per Capita Family
docs.text:
These approaches implement Equal Cumulative Per Capita (ECPC) allocation. When allocation_year is set in the past, cumulative population from that year determines each country's share of the total budget.

Approach Use Case equal-per-capita Year-by-year population shares per-capita-adjusted Additional weighting by pre-allocation responsibility (historical emissions) and capability (GDP) per-capita-adjusted-gini Accounts for within-country inequality

docs.title: Convergence Family
docs.text:
Gradual transition from current emissions to fair share target.

Approach Use Case per-capita-convergence Comparison baseline (not a fair share approach): convergence from current emission levels embeds implicit grandfathering during the transition period Kartha 2018 cumulative-per-capita-convergence Budget-preserving transitions cumulative-per-capita-convergence-adjusted Additional weighting by pre-allocation responsibility (historical emissions) and capability (GDP) cumulative-per-capita-convergence-gini-adjusted Accounts for within-country inequality

docs.title: Choosing an Approach
docs.text:
Question Answer Single target or year-by-year? Budget vs Pathway Account for history via cumulative accounting? Set early allocation_year: cumulative population from that year determines shares Account for history via pre-allocation rescaling? Use -adjusted variants with pre_allocation_responsibility_weight: multiplicative rescaling by emissions in a historical window (per capita by default) Account for capability? Use -adjusted variants with capability_weight: year by year from the allocation year, a snapshot (capability_reference_year) or a cumulative window (capability_window) Account for within-country inequality? Use -gini variants

See Principle to Code for detailed configuration.

Which inequality dataset the -gini approaches use

The default Gini source is the World Bank's Gini index (SI.POV.GINI), which fair-shares fetch-data brings down with everything else. WIID is still available with active_gini_source=unu-wider-2025. It is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO, and those terms travel with every Gini-derived output. The two sources give materially different capability-based allocations; see Data Sources & Licensing.

docs.title: Registry Reference
docs.text:
All approaches are registered in src/fair_shares/library/allocations/manager.py.

Python
from fair_shares.library.allocations.manager import get_allocation_functions

approaches = get_allocation_functions()
print(list(approaches.keys()))

To add an approach, see Adding approaches.

docs.title: Country fair shares
docs.text: Divide a carbon budget or an emissions pathway between individual countries.

docs.title: Which notebook
docs.text:
301_custom_fair_share_allocation is the blank workspace. You set every option in its one configuration cell, then run all cells. If you are new, start from a worked example and change it once it runs:

Notebook What it does 302_example_templates_budget_allocations Budgets: one cumulative number per country. Runs unchanged. 303_example_templates_pathway_allocations Pathways: a value per country per year. Runs unchanged.

Each notebook builds the processed data it needs on its first run, which takes a few minutes. Later runs reuse it. Budget runs (rcbs) also read three files you place by hand once (Files you place yourself).

docs.title: 1. Choose the data
docs.text:
emission_category sets the gases:

Category Covers Notes co2-ffi CO₂ from fossil fuels and industry co2 co2-ffi plus land-use CO₂ National-inventory land use; start years from 2000 all-ghg-ex-co2-lulucf All greenhouse gases except land-use CO₂ GWP100 AR6. Historical PRIMAP data also exclude land-use CH₄ and N₂O all-ghg (default in 301) All greenhouse gases GWP100 AR6; start years from 2000

active_sources["target"] sets what is divided:

Target Approaches Divides rcbs Budget A remaining carbon budget, one cumulative value per country pathway Pathway Scenario pathways such as IPCC AR6 rcb-pathways Pathway A budget turned into a global pathway, then divided year by year (RCB pathway generation)

The other entries of active_sources pick the emissions, population, GDP, Gini and land-use sources. The comments in the cell list the options. Data & licences gives each source's coverage and terms.

docs.title: 2. Choose the approaches
docs.text:
allocations maps each approach to a list of parameter sets. The notebook runs every combination in each set:

Python
allocations = {
    "equal-per-capita-budget": [
        {"allocation_year": [2020], "preserve_allocation_year_shares": [False]}
    ],
    "per-capita-adjusted-budget": [
        {
            "allocation_year": [2020],
            "preserve_allocation_year_shares": [False],
            "pre_allocation_responsibility_weight": [0.5],
            "capability_weight": [0.5],
        }
    ],
}

The second entry shows the structure only. From principle to code has complete worked configurations. For all-ghg, the notebook derives the non-CO₂ pathway approaches from the budget approaches.

Budget approaches: equal-per-capita-budget, per-capita-adjusted-budget (responsibility and capability), per-capita-adjusted-gini-budget (plus inequality within countries).

Pathway approaches: equal-per-capita, per-capita-adjusted, per-capita-adjusted-gini, cumulative-per-capita-convergence and its -adjusted and -gini-adjusted forms, and per-capita-convergence. per-capita-convergence is for comparison only, because convergence from current levels embeds grandfathering during the transition (Kartha 2018).

The Approach catalog describes each approach, and Allocation approaches its parameters. The five entry points of Pelz 2025b help you decide: foundational principles, allocation quantity, allocation approach, indicators, and implications for all others.

docs.title: 3. Read the results
docs.text:
Results land in output/{source_id}/allocations/{allocation_folder}/. A folder of the same name is overwritten.

File Holds allocations_relative.parquet Relative shares, summing to 1 allocations_absolute.parquet Relative share × global target, in Mt CO₂e allocations_wide.csv Wide format for spreadsheets param_manifest.csv Every parameter combination

The approach column separates the approaches. Outputs documents every column.

Negative allocations

A negative allocation means past emissions exceed the allocation. It is an expected result for high historical emitters, for example under equal cumulative per capita from 1990. Negative allocation gives how the literature reads it.

To subtract observed emissions and spread a budget into an annual pathway, see Remaining budgets and annual pathways.

docs.title: Data & licences
docs.text: uv run fair-shares fetch-data downloads most inputs from pinned URLs. The region mapping, the carbon budget table and an example IAMC file ship with the repository. uv run fair-shares fetch-data --list prints the version, licence and citation of every source, and uv run fair-shares cite lists what a run must cite.

docs.title: Can I publish this?
docs.text:
• Results from a default run: yes, for non-commercial use, under share-alike terms. The default emissions source, PRIMAP-hist v2.8, is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and its terms travel with the allocation results. Commercial use needs a licence from the dataset authors.
  • CC BY results: set active_emissions_source to primap-202503 (PRIMAP-hist v2.6.1) or gcb-2025 (fossil CO2 only), and keep the default World Bank Gini. WIID Gini adds non-commercial, share-alike terms to any run.
  • The input data themselves: check each source below.
    • UN WPP population: the UN Terms of Use govern the projection files; check them before republishing population data.
    • AR6 Scenarios Database: research and science communication; no redistribution of substantial parts.
    • Scenario Compass: research use only, under the Nature editorial policies and embargo rules until Riahi et al. is published.
    • ScenarioMIP-CMIP7: research use; no redistribution of substantial parts; state release v0.1 and cite its DOI.
    • CMIP7 historical (IAM regions): share-alike terms on anything derived that you redistribute.
  • Global Carbon Budget 2024 bunkers (opt-in): the Global Carbon Project asks you to cite the original data sources and to consider co-authorship where its data are essential to a study. This is a request, not a licence condition.
  • Always: cite fair-shares and every data source the run used. Each saved run lists them in its CITATIONS.md.

docs.title: PRIMAP-hist v2.8 (default)
docs.text:
Gütschow, J., & Pflüger, M. (2026). The PRIMAP-hist national historical emissions time series (1750-2025) v2.8. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22876287

  • Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, as stated on the Zenodo record. The metadata file inside the record says CC BY-NC 4.0, and fair-shares records the stricter record-level terms. PRIMAP-hist moved to a non-commercial licence with v2.8.
  • Provides: national greenhouse gas emissions, 1750 to 2025. The dataset authors partly extrapolate the latest years. The pipeline uses the country-reported scenario (HISTCR).
  • Location: data/emissions/primap-202609/; a plain fetch-data downloads it.

docs.title: PRIMAP-hist v2.6.1 (opt-in)
docs.text:
Gütschow, J., Busch, D., & Pflüger, M. (2025). The PRIMAP-hist national historical emissions time series (1750-2023) v2.6.1. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.15016289

  • Licence: CC BY 4.0.
  • Provides: national emissions, 1750 to 2023. Select it with active_emissions_source=primap-202503 for CC BY outputs or to reproduce results built on data to 2023.
  • Location: data/emissions/primap-202503/; fetch-data --source primap-202503.

docs.title: Global Carbon Budget 2025 (opt-in)
docs.text:
Andrew, R. M., & Peters, G. P. (2025). The Global Carbon Project's fossil CO2 emissions dataset (2025v15). Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.17417124. Paper: Friedlingstein, P., et al. (2026). Global Carbon Budget 2025. Earth System Science Data, 18, 3211-3288. doi:10.5194/essd-18-3211-2026

  • Licence: CC BY 4.0. Cite both DOIs.
  • Provides: territorial fossil CO2 (co2-ffi only) by country, 1850 to 2024, in Mt CO2 per year. Select it with active_emissions_source=gcb-2025.
  • Location: data/emissions/gcb-2025/; fetch-data --source gcb-2025.

Its processing rules, its coverage rule and the resulting country sets are in Global Carbon Budget processing.

docs.title: Land-use CO2
docs.text: A land-use source carries an accounting basis, and categories with land use (co2, all-ghg) follow it end to end.

docs.title: National inventories (NGHGI basis)
docs.text:
Melo, J., et al. (2026). The LULUCF Data Hub: translating global land use emissions estimates into the national GHG inventory framework. Zenodo. Both releases are CC BY 4.0.

Release Key DOI Coverage Location v4.0.0, 2026 NGHGI release (default) melo-2026-v4 10.5281/zenodo.22828743 Gap-filled, 187 countries, 2000 to 2024 data/lulucf/melo-2026-v4/ v3.1.1, 2025 NGHGI release (opt-in) melo-2026 10.5281/zenodo.18352395 185 countries, 2000 to 2023 data/lulucf/melo-2026/

On this basis the global budget is corrected for the gap between inventory and model land-use accounting (Convention gap).

docs.title: Bookkeeping models (model basis)
docs.text:
Global Carbon Project (2026). Supplemental data of Global Carbon Budget 2025: National Land Use Change Carbon Emissions 2025 v1.0. ICOS Carbon Portal. 10.18160/GCP-2025. Paper: Friedlingstein et al. (2026), 10.5194/essd-18-3211-2026. Cite the bookkeeping-model papers named in each sheet too.

  • Key: gcb-2025-luc. Location: data/lulucf/gcb-2025-luc/.
  • Provides: net land-use change CO2 by country, 1850 to 2024, the mean of the bookkeeping models BLUE, OSCAR and LUCE; the world row is the workbook's Global column. This is how integrated assessment and energy-system models count land-use CO2.
  • On this basis: no convention-gap correction of the global budget; the rebase to 2020 uses bookkeeping land use; AR6 scenario CO2 and Kyoto gases are used as reported.
  • Licence: CC BY 4.0 (ICOS data licence). ICOS asks you to cite the exact DOI or PID, to point your users to ICOS for updates, and to tell the data providers about publications that use the data; the workbook adds that co-authorship may need to be considered when the data are essential to the work.
  • Download (manual): open the ICOS record, click Download, tick the licence confirmation and download. Extract the zip into data/lulucf/gcb-2025-luc/.

docs.title: Population: UN WPP via Our World in Data
docs.text:
United Nations World Population Prospects via Our World in Data (grapher export retrieved 16 October 2026, data to 2023), and UN World Population Prospects 2024 projections. Location: data/population/un-owid-2025/.

Licence: mixed. The UN WPP bulk data files fall under the UN Terms of Use, which are restrictive. The CC BY 3.0 IGO grant documented for WPP covers the report's figures and tables, and not demonstrably the projection files. OWID's own charts and processing are CC BY, but OWID does not relicense upstream data; its historical series splices HYDE, Gapminder and UN WPP, each under its own terms. Check the upstream terms before redistributing.

Coverage. The OWID export starts Ireland in 1950, and about 16 territories after 1850: BES, BLM, BMU, CUW, CYM, GGY, GIB, IMN, MAC, MAF, MNP, NIU, SHN, SXM, VGB and WLF. An allocation that needs population before a country's first year places that country in rest of world.

docs.title: GDP: World Bank WDI
docs.text: World Bank World Development Indicators, export of 8 October 2026. CC BY 4.0. Location: data/gdp/wdi-2025/. It provides GDP in PPP (constant 2021 international dollars) and MER (constant 2015 US dollars), observed to 2025. The choice between PPP and MER is a normative decision that can significantly affect allocation results Pelz 2025b. After 2025 the allocation functions forward-fill GDP per capita (Capability timing).

docs.title: Gini: World Bank WDI (default)
docs.text:
World Bank, World Development Indicators, Gini index (SI.POV.GINI), export of 8 October 2026. The World Bank sources it from its Poverty and Inequality Platform (PIP). No DOI is issued; cite it by name. CC BY 4.0, the World Bank's default for its own open datasets. Location: data/gini/wdi-2025/.

It gives Gini coefficients for 150 countries, each country's latest observation in 2015 to 2023 (selection: latest-available, year_window: [2015, 2023]). Survey-based Gini is sparse in any one year; a single-year rule would cover about 70 countries.

docs.title: Gini: UNU-WIDER WIID (opt-in)
docs.text:
UNU-WIDER World Income Inequality Database (WIID), Version 8 September 2026. doi:10.35188/UNU-WIDER/WIID-080926. Select it with active_gini_source=unu-wider-2025; fetch-data --source unu-wider-2025. Location: data/gini/unu-wider-2025/.

Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO, per UNU-WIDER's copyright terms. The non-commercial and share-alike terms travel with derived Gini values, including a table of them, so a run with WIID gives no CC BY outputs on any emissions source.

It gives Gini coefficients for 194 countries, each country's latest high-quality observation, falling back to the latest of any quality (selection: latest-high-quality, no year window). Coverage is broader than WDI but older: 32 of the 194 values predate 2010, and four are states that no longer exist.

Income and consumption Gini

PIP reports consumption-based Gini for most low- and middle-income countries and income-based Gini elsewhere; WIID pools income-based series. Consumption Gini is systematically lower for the same country-year, and the gap is large for some countries (India 0.255 vs 0.515, Côte d'Ivoire 0.353 vs 0.607, Bangladesh 0.309 vs 0.499, South Africa 0.541 vs 0.670). Higher Gini raises measured capability, so the two sources give materially different capability-based allocations. This is a choice about which welfare concept the capability measure rests on.

A country without a Gini value stays in the analysis with an imputed value (Analysis countries).

docs.title: AR6 reanalysis (Gidden et al. 2023)
docs.text:
Gidden, M. J., et al. (2023). AR6 Scenarios Database hosted by IIASA. doi:10.5281/zenodo.10158920, the v2 record that fetch-data downloads (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8411053 resolves to the latest version). CC BY 4.0. Location: data/scenarios/ipcc_ar6_gidden/.

IPCC AR6 WGIII emission pathways in the national-inventory reanalysis, with the AR6 climate assessment in the metadata. They supply the scenario sets of every budget and the non-CO2 pathways.

docs.title: AR6 Scenarios Database (manual)
docs.text:
Byers, E., Krey, V., Kriegler, E., Riahi, K., et al. (2022). AR6 Scenarios Database (v1.1). IAMC and IIASA. doi:10.5281/zenodo.5886911

Terms: the IIASA AR6 Scenarios Database licence allows use for scientific research and science communication and restricts redistribution of substantial parts. The files are never committed. Two manual inputs come from it, each read from the public database without a login. uv run fair-shares fetch-data --source <key> gives the steps:

  • ipcc_ar6_bunkers (data/scenarios/ipcc_ar6_bunkers/ar6_bunkers_world.csv): world aviation and maritime CO2 of every AR6 scenario that reports them. The database has no bunker variable, so bunkers are 0.6 × aviation plus maritime Weber 2026.
  • ipcc_ar6_climate (data/scenarios/ipcc_ar6_climate/ar6_climate_world.csv): world harmonised-infilled CO2, reported CO2 and the MAGICCv7.5.3 GSAT median and 67th percentile of every AR6 scenario. Notebook 104 derives each scenario's net-zero year and warming at net zero from them (Net zero).

docs.title: Scenario Compass ensemble (manual)
docs.text:
Huppmann, D., Riahi, K., Clarke, L., Hasegawa, T., et al. (2026). Scenario Compass Initiative - Pathways Ensemble 2026 (v2.0). Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.23232097. Release v1.0: Huppmann, D., et al. (2026). Scenario Compass Initiative - Pathways Ensemble 2025 (v1.0). doi:10.5281/zenodo.18598251. Manuscript: Riahi, K., et al. (2026). Mitigation benchmarks from the 2025 community update of global emissions pathways. Research Square preprint. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-8891091/v1

Terms: IAMC licence. The workbook states: "The data may be used for scientific research purposes. However, users must strictly adhere to the applicable Nature editorial policies and embargo rules until the manuscript has been formally published." The file is never committed or redistributed.

Location: data/scenarios/sci-2026-v2.0/SCI-2026_v2.0_pathways_ensemble_global.xlsx (sci-2026, download from the Scenario Compass platform with a login). Release v1.0 sits at data/scenarios/sci-2025-v1.0/ (sci-2025). The version key of the sci entry in scenario_sources.yaml selects the release.

Provides: scenarios that report bunkers, for the bunker share, and, opt-in, scenarios for the non-CO2 set. Scenario sets gives what it contributes and how its warming at net zero is derived.

docs.title: ScenarioMIP-CMIP7 ensemble (manual)
docs.text:
Riahi, K., van Vuuren, D., et al. (2026). Scenario data of the 'Socioeconomic, Emissions and Land Use Futures - The ScenarioMIP Pathways for CMIP7' (v0.1). Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22296051

Terms: copyright 2026 IIASA and contributing modeling teams. Use for scientific research is allowed; redistribution of substantial parts is prohibited. Every result states release v0.1 and cites the DOI. The file is never committed or redistributed.

Location: data/scenarios/scenariomip-v0.1/ScenarioMIP_v0.1_global.xlsx (scenariomip-cmip7, download from the ScenarioMIP Explorer after registration).

Provides: runs with international aviation and shipping CO2, in the default bunker-share pool, and opt-in scenarios for the non-CO2 set (Bunker share).

docs.title: CMIP7 ScenarioMIP historical (IAM regions)
docs.text:
Nicholls, Z., Kikstra, J., Zecchetto, M., & Hoegner, A. (2025). CMIP7 ScenarioMIP historical timeseries for harmonisation and simple climate model workflow (2025.12.07). Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.17845154

Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0. The Zenodo record metadata say CC0; the dataset authors confirmed that the share-alike licence is deliberate. Its share-alike terms apply to anything you redistribute that is derived from it. Provides: country-level historical emissions that notebook 400 aggregates to model regions to back-fill an IAM scenario (src/fair_shares/conf/data_sources/iamc_data_sources.yaml). It combines CEDS, GFED/BB4CMIP7, the Global Carbon Budget and published inversions for HFCs and ozone-depleting substances; cite those component datasets too when you report values derived from it. Location: data/emissions/cmip7-historical-2025.12.07/; fetch-data --all or on first use.

docs.title: Published carbon budgets
docs.text:
data/rcbs/rcbs.yaml holds five published sources. The budget label, temperature and likelihood of each are in Remaining carbon budgets.

Source 1.5 °C, 50% Budget from Notes Lamboll 2023 250 Gt CO2 2023 Methodology paper for updated budget estimates Forster 2024 200 Gt CO2 2024 IGCC 2023 Forster 2026 130 Gt CO2 2026 IGCC 2025, Table 8; also 1.7 °C and 2 °C IPCC 2021 SPM (ar6_2020, ar6_wg1_2021) 500 Gt CO2 2020 Table SPM.2; ar6_wg1_2021 adds 1.7 °C and 2 °C

The choice of budget (source, temperature and likelihood) is entry point 2 of the fair share quantification framework, the allocation quantity Pelz 2025b. Results are sensitive to it, so report all three with every result.

docs.title: Global Carbon Budget 2025 global workbook (manual)
docs.text: Global Carbon Project (2026). Supplemental data of Global Carbon Budget 2025 (Version 1.1). doi:10.18160/GCP-2025, with the GCB 2025 paper above. CC BY 4.0 (ICOS CCBY4 Data Licence). Location: data/emissions/gcb-2025/Global_Carbon_Budget_2025_v1.0.xlsx (gcb-2025-global, behind the ICOS licence page). It provides observed global net CO2 (fossil minus cement carbonation plus bookkeeping land use), which expresses each budget from the start of 2020.

docs.title: Global Carbon Budget 2024 (opt-in bunkers)
docs.text:
Paper: Friedlingstein, P., et al. (2025). Global Carbon Budget 2024. Earth System Science Data, 17, 965-1039. doi:10.5194/essd-17-965-2025. Data: Global Carbon Project (2024). Supplemental data of Global Carbon Budget 2024 (Version 1.0). doi:10.18160/GCP-2024. Location: data/bunkers/gcb-2024/.

Licence: the paper is CC BY 4.0. The data product is not CC-licensed. It carries the Global Carbon Project's terms of use, which ask that the original data sources be cited alongside it, and note that where the data are essential to a study, co-authorship may need to be considered. That is a request from the providers, not a licence condition. Cite both DOIs; the paper DOI is not the data DOI.

Each emissions source names its bunker data (bunkers_source in data_sources_unified.yaml). The default is the Global Carbon Budget 2025 file; this workbook stays available as bunkers_source: gcb-2024 (Bunker deduction).

docs.title: Regions
docs.text: regioniso3c, a custom mapping by Setu Pelz (2024), MIT, in data/regions/. It maps ISO3 country codes to model regions and converts country outputs to regions. IAMC workflows use the regions defined in your input file instead (IAM model regions).

docs.title: Citing
docs.text:
Cite fair-shares (CITATION.cff is the source of truth) and every data source a run used:

Bash
uv run fair-shares cite            # as text
uv run fair-shares cite --bibtex   # as BibTeX entries

To add a source, see Adding data sources.

docs.title: The ESABCC presets
docs.text:
This guide computes remaining budgets for EU countries, the EU27 and the EEA with the settings of the ESABCC 2023 advice (ESABCC 2023; Pelz 2023). The preset esabcc_2023_allocations() holds those settings. Several library defaults differ from them, so use the preset rather than building the runs by hand. ESABCC 2023 reproduction compares the results with the original study.

Before you start, fetch the input data and the three manual files (Install and data).

docs.title: Run one allocation
docs.text:
The example takes the first run of the co2-ffi grid: equal per capita from 1990. It uses the settings of notebook 601_reproduce_esabcc_2023, section 3.

Python
from fair_shares.library.presets import (
    ESABCC_2023_RCB_ANCHOR,
    esabcc_2023_allocation_list,
)
from fair_shares.library.python_api import calculate_allocation_timeseries

EU27 = [
    "AUT", "BEL", "BGR", "CYP", "CZE", "DEU", "DNK", "ESP", "EST", "FIN",
    "FRA", "GRC", "HRV", "HUN", "IRL", "ITA", "LTU", "LUX", "LVA", "MLT",
    "NLD", "POL", "PRT", "ROU", "SVK", "SVN", "SWE",
]
EEA = EU27 + ["ISL", "NOR"]  # Liechtenstein is in rest of world

allocations = esabcc_2023_allocation_list("co2-ffi")

result = calculate_allocation_timeseries(
    emission_category="co2-ffi",
    allocation=allocations[0],
    rcb_source=ESABCC_2023_RCB_ANCHOR["source"],
    climate_assessment=ESABCC_2023_RCB_ANCHOR["climate-assessment"],
    quantile=ESABCC_2023_RCB_ANCHOR["quantile"],
    shape="half-sine",
    deviation_end_year=2050,
    convergence_year=2050,
    nonco2_debt_mode=None,
    pathway_end_year=2100,
    base_share_floor_mt=0.001,
    desired_harmonisation_year=2020,
    emissions_source="primap-202609",
    gdp_source="wdi-2025",
    population_source="un-owid-2025",
    gini_source="wdi-2025",
    lulucf_source="melo-2026-v4",
    allocation_folder="eu-budgets",
)

pathways = result.allocation_timeseries
iso3c = pathways.index.get_level_values("iso3c")
future = [c for c in pathways.columns if int(c) > result.netting_end_year]
remaining = pathways[future].sum(axis=1).groupby(iso3c).sum() / 1000  # Gt CO2

print(f"Remaining from {result.netting_end_year + 1}:")
print("EU27", round(remaining[EU27].sum(), 1), "Gt CO2")
print("EEA ", round(remaining[EEA].sum(), 1), "Gt CO2")

The first run builds the processed data and takes a few minutes. allocations holds 36 runs for co2-ffi. Loop over it to compute every approach of the study.

docs.title: What the result holds
docs.text:
result.allocation_timeseries has one row per country. Its index holds iso3c and the identifying columns listed in Outputs. Its columns are the years to pathway_end_year. The years after result.netting_end_year sum to the remaining budget. remaining in the example is a Series of remaining budgets in Gt CO2, indexed by iso3c. Summing it over a list of ISO3 codes gives a group total, as the example does for the EU27 and the EEA.

The library allocates to countries. The EU27 and EEA values are sums of their members. For the responsibility approaches this differs from allocating to the EU27 as one region, as the original study did (Reproduction accuracy).

Each country's annual pathway to pathway_end_year sums to its remaining budget. The remaining budget is the allocation minus observed emissions from the allocation year to netting_end_year, the last observed year: 2025 for co2-ffi. A remaining budget can be negative when past emissions exceed the allocation. shape, deviation_end_year and convergence_year set how the pathway spreads the budget over time. They are normative choices (Python API).

Countries without complete data fall into rest of world and get no row of their own. Liechtenstein has no GDP series, so it is in rest of world and missing from the EEA sum. country_data_coverage_summary.csv in the processed folder names every country in rest of world.

docs.title: Other categories
docs.text: The preset also covers all-ghg-ex-co2-lulucf and all-ghg. Both allocate from 2015 only, and all-ghg starts its responsibility window in 2000, where national land-use data begin. For these categories pass nonco2_debt_mode, one of "report-only" or "co2-debit". Greenhouse gases explains the two modes.

docs.title: IAM model regions
docs.text: Use this guide when your data is an IAMC-format scenario file and you want to divide a budget or a pathway between that model's regions. For individual countries, use Country fair shares. For a model of one region, such as an EU-only model, see One region of countries.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the scenario with notebook 400
docs.text:
400_data_preprocess_scenario_for_allocation reads your scenario, adds the history an allocation needs and writes output/iamc/iamc_covered.xlsx. Notebooks 401, 402 and 403 read that file. They fail with a missing-file error if you skip notebook 400.

Set four values in the Config cell:

Setting What to give SCENARIO_FILE Your IAMC file. It points at the bundled MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM example by default, and notebook 400 runs on that example without error if you forget to change it. MODEL_NAME The model's name as it appears in IAMconsortium/common-definitions, for example MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM 2.1-R12. The notebook reads the country-to-region mapping from there. EMISSION_CATEGORY all-ghg-ex-co2-lulucf, the only supported category. START_YEAR The first year of history to add, 1990 by default. It must be no later than your allocation year.

Your file needs these variables for every model region:

  • Emissions|CO2|Energy and Industrial Processes
  • Emissions|CH4
  • Emissions|N2O
  • Population
  • GDP|PPP

Notebook 400 adds CEDS-based regional emissions history, UN and OWID population and World Bank WDI GDP before your scenario starts. It then builds Emissions|Covered: CO2 from energy and industry plus CH4 and N2O, weighted with AR6 GWP100, in Mt CO2e per year. Land-use emissions are out of scope. F-gases exist in the historical source at World level only. Expect a step at the join year between your model's output and the history.

Region patches. common-definitions can lack ISO3 codes that the CEDS history covers. Add them to a region with mapping.add_countries(...). The example cell patches five small territories for the R12 regions. Remove or replace that cell for another model.

The output holds one model and one scenario. Notebook 400 labels every row with the first model and scenario name in your file, and interpolates all values to annual years.

docs.title: 2. Allocate
docs.text:
Notebook What it does 402_example_iamc_budget_allocations Worked budget examples, one cumulative number per region. Runs unchanged. 403_example_iamc_pathway_allocations Worked pathway examples, a value per region per year. Runs unchanged. 401_custom_iamc_allocation Workspace you configure yourself, with export of a model-ready remaining budget.

The regions are whatever your file holds. Read them from the file, because they often carry a model prefix such as MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM 2.1-R12|Western Europe:

Python
import pyam
from fair_shares.library.allocations.budgets.per_capita import equal_per_capita_budget
from fair_shares.library.utils.data.iamc import load_iamc_data

scenario = pyam.IamDataFrame("output/iamc/iamc_covered.xlsx")
regions = [r for r in scenario.region if r.lower() not in ("world", "global")]

data = load_iamc_data(
    data_file=scenario,
    population_variable="Population",
    gdp_variable="GDP|PPP",
    emissions_variable="Emissions|Covered",
    regions=regions,
    allocation_start_year=1990,
    budget_end_year=2100,
    expand_to_annual=True,
)

result = equal_per_capita_budget(
    population_ts=data["population"].rename_axis(index={"region": "iso3c"}),
    allocation_year=2015,
    emission_category="all-ghg-ex-co2-lulucf",
    preserve_allocation_year_shares=False,
    group_level="iso3c",
)
shares = result.relative_shares_cumulative_emission["2015"]

per_capita_adjusted_budget takes gdp_ts=data["gdp"] in the same way. The Approach catalog lists the approaches.

load_iamc_data stops with an error when any region lacks a value in the start year or the end year.

docs.title: 3. Export a remaining budget for your model
docs.text:
Step 7 of notebook 401 turns a budget allocation into a remaining budget for a model run. The global budget is the scenario's own cumulative Emissions|Covered from the allocation year to MODEL_HORIZON_YEAR. Each region's remaining budget is its share of that total minus its emissions from the allocation year to the year before the first model period. Those emissions come from iamc_covered.xlsx: history up to the scenario's first year, the scenario's own values after it.

IAM models label each period by its last year. In MESSAGEix with 5-year periods, timestep 2030 covers 2026 to 2030. The remaining budget must start in the first year of the first period, so set FIRST_MODEL_TIMESTEP and TIMESTEP_LENGTH:

Text Only
Remaining budget (from 2026) = allocation (from 2015) - emissions (2015 to 2025)

The notebook writes iamc_remaining_budget_from_<year>_<approach>.csv in Gt CO2e, for use as a cumulative emissions bound such as bound_emission in MESSAGEix. Pathway allocations are already annual. Use their Step 6 export directly.

docs.title: Negative allocations
docs.text: A negative remaining budget means the region's past emissions exceed its allocation. It is an expected result for high historical emitters, for example under equal cumulative per capita from 1990 (Negative allocation). In a model run it can call for a net-negative emissions target. It does not prescribe timing or mechanism. Keep negative values rather than clipping them to zero, so the result keeps that information Pelz 2025a; Pelz 2025b.

docs.title: One region of countries
docs.text:
Notebooks 400 to 403 divide a budget between the regions of an IAMC file, so the file must cover the world. A model of one region, such as an EU-only energy model, has no data for the rest of the world. 405_one_region_remaining_budget serves that case and needs no IAMC input. It allocates the global budget between countries with the country datasets, then sums the countries of your region. It reports the region and each member country.

The settings are in three cells: A. Your model (everyone edits), B. Budget and region (check), C. Advanced (usually left as is).

docs.title: A. Your model
docs.text:
Setting What to give IAMC_MODEL, IAMC_REGION Your model's name and region name, as in its IAMC files. EMISSION_CATEGORY co2 (default): a CO2 budget, cumulative to net-zero CO2, covering fossil, industry and land-use CO2. co2-ffi: a budget of fossil and industry CO2 only, for a model without land use, plus the land-use condition it rests on (below). all-ghg: the same CO2 budget plus an annual non-CO2 pathway (CH4, N2O, F-gases; CO2-equivalent with AR6 GWP100). CO2_VARIABLE Your model's variable for the CO2 the budget bounds, for example Emissions|CO2. LAND_USE_BASIS model (default) or inventory; see below. FIRST_MODEL_TIMESTEP, TIMESTEP_LENGTH Your model's first period, labelled by its last year: 2030 with 5 covers 2026-2030. The budget is given from the first year of that period. NON_CO2_VARIABLE, NONCO2_DEBT_MODES all-ghg only, commented out by default. Your model's variable for the non-CO2 gases, and how past non-CO2 over-use is settled: report-only leaves the CO2 budget as it is, co2-debit subtracts the region's over-use (summed over the members that over-used). Each mode is its own scenario.

Land-use basis. Models and national greenhouse gas inventories (NGHGI) count land-use CO2 differently: inventories count part of the natural land sink as a removal, models do not.

LAND_USE_BASIS Land-use source The run then uses Use it to model (default) gcb-2025-luc: bookkeeping models (GCB 2025 national land-use change), 1850-2024 country history with bookkeeping land use; the global budget with no inventory correction, rebased with bookkeeping land use; scenario CO2 and Kyoto gases as reported bound your model's own CO2 inventory melo-2026-v4: national inventories (LULUCF Data Hub v4), 2000-2024 country history with inventory land use; the global budget corrected for the inventory-versus-model gap; NGHGI-adjusted scenario CO2 and Kyoto gases compare with inventory-based targets, such as the EU Climate Law

gcb-2025-luc is a manual download; fair-shares fetch-data prints the steps.

Land-use condition (co2-ffi). The fossil-only budget removes the projected global land-use CO2 from the budget's first year to net zero, on the bookkeeping basis. A projected net sink counts as zero (the precautionary cap), so the world's fossil budget takes no credit for future land sinks (Land-use term for fossil CO₂). A region's or member's fossil budget is then a fair share only if its own bookkeeping land-use CO2 over those years nets to at most its allowance: its share of the global allocation times the removed term, zero under the cap. A net source above the allowance comes off the fossil budget; a sink beyond it is not counted. The run prints, per area, the allowance and observed land-use CO2 for 2020 to 2024 on both bases, with the indirect gap (inventory minus bookkeeping). In inventory terms the allowance means holding an inventory sink of about the indirect gap: for the EU27, -214 to -241 Mt CO2 per year over 2020 to 2024. A net sink is also needed when the model nets residual fossil CO2 against land at net zero, when the cap is turned off, and when the fair share is already used up; for the last, use co2, where land use counts.

First model period. The budget is first netted with observed emissions through the last observed year. If the model's first period starts earlier, the region's observed emissions in the period are added back. If it starts later, the region's emissions in the years before it are subtracted; years without observed data take the last observed year's value, and the run and the output name those years.

docs.title: B. Budget and region
docs.text: Setting What to give RCB_SOURCE, TEMPERATURE_LIKELIHOOD The published budget set and one or more (warming level, likelihood) pairs. Default forster_2026, [(1.7, 0.5), (2, 0.9)]: 748 and 848 Gt CO2 from 2020, bracketing a global budget of 800 Gt from 2020. The run prints every published budget counted from 2020, so you can match a budget fixed elsewhere, and stops with the available pairs if one is not published. REGION_NAME, REGION_COUNTRIES The region's name and its members' ISO3 codes. EU27 is preset.

docs.title: C. Advanced
docs.text: Setting What to give ALLOCATIONS Approaches and parameter grids, as in notebook 301. The non-CO2 pathway follows the same approach. The defaults: equal cumulative per capita from 2015; from 2020, responsibility for emissions per person since 2015, capability, and the two combined (0.4 and 0.6, with a development threshold of 7,500 dollars per person). Responsibility is per capita: absolute responsibility divides by a country's total emissions, which favours small countries for their size and makes a region's total depend on how it splits into countries. IAMC_SCENARIO_PREFIX, CO2_MAGNITUDE, OUTPUT_LABEL Scenario names, the CO2 budget in Gt or Mt, the output folder. active_sources The fair-shares default data sources. The land-use source follows LAND_USE_BASIS.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
In output/<OUTPUT_LABEL>/:

  • <REGION_NAME>_targets.csv: one row per configuration for the region and for each member (iso3c), with every configuration column, the CO2 budget before and after the non-CO2 debit, the first-period adjustment, and the annual non-CO2 pathway.
  • <REGION_NAME>_land_use_condition.csv, for co2-ffi: the allowance and observed land-use CO2 per area, budget and approach.
  • <REGION_NAME>_targets_iamc.xlsx: one scenario per budget, approach and debt mode; the region under IAMC_REGION, each member under its ISO3 code. The CO2 row has unit Gt CO2 (no /yr) and sits at the first year of the model's first period; the non-CO2 rows are annual, Mt CO2e/yr. The meta sheet records the land-use basis, the first model period, the parameters and the member countries.

  • <REGION_NAME>_targets_iamc_model_periods.xlsx, for all-ghg: the same with the non-CO2 pathway as averages over the model's periods, labelled by their last year.

  • columns.csv: the meaning and unit of every column of the CSV files; each IAMC file has the same in a columns sheet (Output columns).

A member without data in the country sets is aggregated into rest of world; the run then stops and names it.

The parquet files hold every result with its identifiers, data sources, parameters, year columns and quality flags. Output columns gives the meaning and unit of every column, and each output folder holds columns.csv with the entries of its own columns.

Python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_parquet("allocations_relative.parquet")
