docs.title: Pipeline map
docs.text: This page follows one allocation run from raw input files to saved results. Each row names the notebook that does the work, the library code behind it, and the files it writes. Use it to find where a number comes from, or where to change a step.

docs.title: The run in one picture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    U["Your notebook: 301 / 302 / 303 / 601<br/>set sources, category, approaches"] --> S["setup_data()<br/>writes output/<source-id>/config.yaml"]
    S --> SM["Snakemake (Snakefile)<br/>reruns everything when the provenance stamp differs"]
    SM --> P1["101 emissions"]
    SM --> P2["102 GDP"]
    SM --> P3["103 population"]
    SM --> P4["105 Gini"]
    SM --> P5["107 NGHGI LULUCF<br/>(co2, all-ghg)"]
    SM --> P6["108 bunkers<br/>(budget runs)"]
    P1 --> P5
    P5 --> P7["104 AR6 scenarios<br/>(scenario adjustments, non-CO2)"]
    P7 -. "rcb-pathways only" .-> P8["106 budget to world pathway"]
    P1 & P2 & P3 & P4 & P5 & P6 & P7 & P8 --> M["100 master step<br/>100_rcbs (budgets) or 100_pathways"]
    M --> A["Back in your notebook:<br/>run_all_allocations()"]
    A --> O["output/<source-id>/allocations/<folder>/<br/>parquet + CSV + CITATIONS.md"]

You run one notebook. That notebook calls setup_data(), which writes a run configuration and calls Snakemake. Snakemake runs the preprocessing notebooks in the order their inputs require. Control then returns to your notebook, which runs the allocations and saves the results.

setup_data() reuses an existing output/<source-id>/ folder only when its provenance stamp matches. The stamp is output/<source-id>/.provenance_stamp.json. It hashes the package version, the run config, the preprocessing notebooks, the Snakefile, the preprocessing library code, the packaged config files, data/rcbs/rcbs.yaml and the registry checksums of the input files. When any of these change, setup_data() reruns all preprocessing for the folder and logs which components changed. Set FAIR_SHARES_TRUST_CACHE=1 or pass trust_cache=True to reuse the folder without the check.

docs.title: 1. Configuration
docs.text:
What Where Writes Choose sources, emission category, target, approaches Top cells of notebook 301, 302, 303 or 601 (in memory) Validate the choices, compose the run config setup_data() in library/utils/data/setup.py; rule compose_config output/<source-id>/config.yaml Source definitions and defaults src/fair_shares/conf/data_sources/data_sources_unified.yaml Budget sources and rebase settings data/rcbs/rcbs.yaml Step order and which notebook runs for which settings Snakefile Input file versions, checksums, licences src/fair_shares/conf/data_registry.yaml; fair-shares fetch-data data/PROVENANCE.md

The <source-id> folder name joins the active sources, the target and the category, for example primap-202609_wdi-2025_un-owid-2025_wdi-2025_rcbs_co2-ffi. Two runs with different sources therefore never overwrite each other.

docs.title: 2. Preprocessing (run by Snakemake)
docs.text:
Notebooks with a source name in the file name come in one copy per source. The Snakefile picks the copy that matches the active source. Notebooks without one serve every source of their kind: 101_data_preprocess_emiss_primap reads every PRIMAP-hist release, and 107_derive_lulucf_categories every LULUCF source. The executed copy under output/<source-id>/notebooks/ keeps the source name.

Notebook Snakemake rule Runs when Does Writes (under output/<source-id>/intermediate/) 101_data_preprocess_emiss_primap, 101_data_preprocess_emiss_gcb-2025 preprocess_emiss always Reads historical emissions (PRIMAP-hist or GCB 2025) and builds one series per emission category emissions/emiss_<category>_timeseries.csv 102_data_preprocess_gdp_<source> preprocess_gdp always GDP in constant 2021 PPP dollars (World Bank WDI) gdp/gdp_timeseries.csv 103_data_preprocess_population_<source> preprocess_population always Population history and UN WPP 2024 projections population/population_timeseries.csv 105_data_preprocess_gini_<source> preprocess_gini always Gini index (WDI by default, WIID opt-in) gini/gini_stationary.csv 107_derive_lulucf_categories preprocess_lulucf category co2 or all-ghg Adds national-inventory (NGHGI) land-use CO2 from the LULUCF Data Hub. Builds co2, non-co2 and all-ghg history emissions/emiss_co2_timeseries.csv and related files 108_data_preprocess_bunkers_<source> preprocess_bunkers budget targets Observed international aviation and shipping CO2 from the Global Carbon Budget (gcb-2025 by default) emissions/bunker_timeseries.csv 104_data_preprocess_scenarios_ar6 preprocess_scenarios and related rules scenario-based targets, all budget runs with active_scenario_source: ar6, and every multi-gas run AR6 scenario pathways, harmonised to history. Selects the scenario sets of every budget, computes the land-use terms and the bunker share, and builds the non-CO2 pathway of each budget scenarios/scenarios_<category>_timeseries.csv, scenarios/scenarios_<category>_by_budget_timeseries.csv, scenarios/rcb_scenario_adjustments.yaml, scenarios/scenario_set_<source>_<label>.csv, scenarios/bunker_share_reporters.csv 106_generate_pathways_from_rcbs generate_rcb_pathways target rcb-pathways Turns a global budget into a world pathway (exponential decay by default) scenarios/scenarios_<category>_timeseries.csv 100_data_preprocess_rcbs master_preprocess budget targets Joins all inputs, fixes the analysis-country set and rest of world, rebases each budget to 2020 processed/rcbs_<category>.csv, processed/country_*.csv, processed/world_*.csv, processed/country_data_coverage_summary.csv 100_data_preprocess_pathways master_preprocess pathway targets, and the non-CO2 part of multi-gas runs The same join, for annual pathways processed/...

The master step calls the library functions in library/pipeline/preprocessing.py (run_rcb_preprocessing, run_pathway_preprocessing, run_non_co2_preprocessing). Budget rebasing lives in library/utils/data/rcb.py and library/preprocessing/rcbs.py. The scenario sets and the bunker share live in library/utils/data/scenario_sets.py, and the scenario source registry in library/utils/data/scenario_sources.py with src/fair_shares/conf/scenario_sources.yaml. The analysis-country rule lives in library/preprocessing/coverage.py, and rest of world in library/preprocessing/row.py. Remaining carbon budgets explains the rebasing and the NGHGI corrections, and Greenhouse gases the multi-gas split.

Notebook 104 reads the scenario sources in src/fair_shares/conf/scenario_sources.yaml and the observed global CO2 named in rcbs.yaml. Four of these inputs are manual. fair-shares fetch-data --source <name> gives the steps for each one. Files you place yourself lists every manual input.

docs.title: 3. Allocation (back in your notebook)
docs.text:
What Where Load the processed inputs load_allocation_data() in library/notebook_helpers.py Expand the parameter grid, run every approach run_all_allocations() in library/notebook_helpers.py, which calls run_allocation() in library/allocations/manager.py Approach registry (name to function) get_allocation_functions() in library/allocations/manager.py Budget approaches library/allocations/budgets/per_capita.py Pathway approaches library/allocations/pathways/ Shared maths (adjustments, convergence) library/utils/math/ Save results with metadata library/allocations/results/

Results land in output/<source-id>/allocations/<allocation_folder>/ as parquet and wide CSV, together with the run's CITATIONS.md. The column meanings are in Output Schema.

docs.title: 4. Remaining budgets and annual pathways (notebook 601 and the Python API)
docs.text: Notebook 601 goes two steps further than the allocation itself. Section 5 subtracts each country's observed emissions from its allocated budget, which gives the budget remaining from the year after the last observed year. A run nets every part through the last year that all its parts observe: 2025 for co2-ffi on the default sources (remaining from 2026), and 2024 for all-ghg, whose land-use data end in 2024 (remaining from 2025). Section 6 spreads each remaining budget into an annual pathway to 2100. The same two steps are available without the notebook through calculate_allocation_timeseries() in library/python_api.py (Python API). A test (tests/integration/test_python_api_reproduces_notebook.py) checks that the notebook and the API give the same numbers.

docs.title: The IAM-region route (400 series)
docs.text:
Notebook Does Writes 400_data_preprocess_scenario_for_allocation Reads a raw IAMC scenario file, adds regional history for emissions, population and GDP, builds Emissions|Covered output/iamc/iamc_covered.xlsx 401_custom_iamc_allocation Your own IAM-region allocation; also exports a model-ready budget output/iamc/... 402_example_iamc_budget_allocations, 403_example_iamc_pathway_allocations Worked examples output/iamc/... 405_one_region_remaining_budget Fair-share targets for one region of countries (such as EU27), for a model without rest-of-world data: a CO2 budget (total or fossil only, with its land-use condition) and, for all-GHG, an annual non-CO2 pathway, in the model's variable names, for the region and each member. Allocates between countries and sums the members output/405_<label>/ (tidy CSV, IAMC xlsx)

The history back-fill lives in library/iamc_historical/. These notebooks run outside Snakemake. Run 400 before 401 to 403; 405 needs no IAMC input.

docs.title: Reproductions of published studies (600 series)
docs.text:
Notebook Study Status 601_reproduce_esabcc_2023 ESABCC (2023) and the underlying IIASA study, Pelz, Rogelj and Riahi (2023) Same approaches and parameters, current data. 602_reproduce_dekker_2025 Dekker et al. (2025) Four of six approaches, expressed in library terms 604_reproduce_vandenberg_2020 van den Berg et al. (2020) Effort-sharing approaches, expressed in library terms 605_reproduce_matthews_2016 Gignac and Matthews (2015), Matthews (2016) Carbon-debt formulation, expressed in library terms

These notebooks show that the library can express each study's method. Each one lists the input differences that would have to be removed before its numbers could match the study's published figures.

docs.title: Updating data each year
docs.text: Most inputs have a new release every year: PRIMAP-hist, the Global Carbon Budget, the LULUCF Data Hub, World Bank WDI, UN population and the indicators behind the remaining carbon budgets. This guide moves a run to a new release. Adding data sources covers a source the library has never used.

docs.title: 1. See what you have
docs.text:
Bash
uv run fair-shares fetch-data --list     # source, version, size, licence
uv run fair-shares fetch-data --verify   # re-hash the files you have

docs.title: 2. Register the new release
docs.text:
Each release is its own source with its own key, such as primap-202609 for PRIMAP-hist v2.8. Keep the old key, so earlier results stay reproducible.

  1. Add a registry entry to src/fair_shares/conf/data_registry.yaml: URL, checksum, licence, citation and tier. Check the licence again. PRIMAP-hist moved from CC BY to CC BY-NC-SA between releases.
  2. Record each DOI you verified in tests/fixtures/verified_dois.yaml, and place a CITATION.md in the data folder.
  3. Add the source to src/fair_shares/conf/data_sources/data_sources_unified.yaml. A new PRIMAP-hist release reuses 101_data_preprocess_emiss_primap through the notebook key, so it needs no new notebook.
  4. Run uv run fair-shares fetch-data --source <key>, then --verify.

Registering the source gives the details and the tests that check each step.

docs.title: 3. Sources without a version number
docs.text: The World Bank and Our World in Data overwrite their exports in place. --verify reports a changed file as drift, not as damage. Re-download with uv run fair-shares fetch-data --source <key> --force, then update its reference_sha256 in the registry. PROVENANCE.md records the hash of the file you used.

docs.title: 4. Update the budget inputs
docs.text: Budgets are rebased to 2020 with observed global CO2 from the Global Carbon Budget global workbook. A new workbook is a manual download (Files you place yourself). Point observed_co2_path in data/rcbs/rcbs.yaml at it. New published budgets, such as a new year of the Indicators of Global Climate Change, are entries under rcb_data in the same file (Remaining carbon budgets).

docs.title: 5. Run with the new release
docs.text:
Name the new key in the active_sources of your notebook or Python call. The library defaults sit in the notebooks and in src/fair_shares/library/preprocessing/config.py.

Each processed folder carries a provenance stamp: hashes of the package version, the run configuration, the preprocessing code, rcbs.yaml and the input files. A changed stamp rebuilds the folder on the next run, and the log names what changed. FAIR_SHARES_TRUST_CACHE=1 reuses a folder without the check.

docs.title: 6. Check the result
docs.text:
• country_data_coverage_summary.csv in the processed folder lists the analysis countries and rest of world. A new release can move a country between them.
  • The last observed year sets the year from which budgets remain (Remaining budgets and annual pathways).
  • uv run fair-shares cite lists the citations and licences of the new run.
